THE MAINE DEPARTMENT OF CORRECTIONS (MDOC) IS COMMITTED TO A NEW MODEL OF CORRECTIONS, PROMOTING THE SAFETY AND WELL-BEING OF STAFF AND RESIDENTS, WHILE ENSURING RESIDENTS AND COMMUNITY CLIENTS SEE FEWER BARRIERS AS THEY ENGAGE WITH REHABILITATIVE-FOCUSED SERVICES. THIS PHILOSOPHY, KNOWN AS THE MAINE MODEL OF CORRECTIONS, IS FOUNDED ON PRINCIPLES OF NORMALIZATION AND HUMANIZATION, WITH EMPHASIS ON DESTIGMATIZATION, RESPECT, AND MODERNIZATION. SIMPLY, THE GOAL IS TO REBUILD AND TRANSFORM LIVES. 

THE NATIONAL STATE OF EMERGENCY WILL END MAY 2023, A SIGNIFICANT NUMBER OF MDOC RESIDENTS WHO QUALIFY FOR MAINECARE UPON RELEASE WILL NO LONGER BE ELIGIBLE. THE HEALTH CARE MARKETPLACE WILL PROVIDE A OPTION FOR HEALTH INSURANCE, BUT INCARCERATED PERSONS ARE NOT ELIGIBLE TO APPLY UNTIL AFTER RELEASED INTO THE COMMUNITY. WITHOUT HEALTH INSURANCE, THE ABILITY TO COVER TREATMENT AND MEDICATION FOR COMMUNITY-BASED OPIOID USE DISORDER TREATMENT SERVICES WILL BE LIMITED OR NON-EXISTENT. AS STUDIES SHOW, THE RISK OF DEATH FROM AN OPIOID OVERDOSE TWO WEEKS AFTER COMMUNITY REENTRY IS GREATER THAN 40% COMPARED TO THE RISK OF DEATH IN THE GENERAL POPULATION. AT ONE-YEAR POST-RELEASE THE RISK OF OPIOID-RELATED FATAL OVERDOSE FOR FORMERLY INCARCERATED INDIVIDUALS IS 11% GREATER THAN THE RISK FOR THOSE IN THE GENERAL POPULATION.

TO REDUCE OVERDOSE AND RELAPSE, MDOC WILL PARTNER WITH GROUPS RECOVER TOGETHER FOR COUNSELING, TREATMENT, AND MEDICATION FOR RESIDENTS UP TO 8-WEEKS POST-RELEASE. A RESEARCH AND EVALUATION PARTNER WILL BE IDENTIFIED THROUGH A REQUEST FOR APPLICATIONS (RFA) TO COMPETE MONTHLY, QUARTERLY, AND YEARLY ANALYSIS OF THE PROJECT. THE TARGET POPULATION WILL INCLUDE RESIDENTS RECEIVING MEDICATIONS FOR SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER (MSUD) TREATMENT, THOSE RELEASING FROM THE REENTRY CENTERS, AND THOSE WHO DO NOT HAVE ACCESS TO MAINECARE AT TIME OF RELEASE. 

THE PROJECT IDENTIFIES FIVE GOALS: 1) INCREASED ACCESS TO COMMUNITY-BASED MSUD SERVICES FOR RESIDENTS REENTERING FROM SECURE CONFINEMENT; 2) REDUCE BARRIERS TO MSUD TREATMENT INCLUDING ACCESS TO INTERNET, PHONES, TRANSPORTATION; 3) REDUCE RISK OF FATAL OVERDOSE UPON RELEASE FROM SECURE CONFINEMENT; 4) REDUCE OVERALL RECIDIVISM OVER THREE-YEARS BY 2%; AND 5) REDUCE SUBSTANCE USE CRIME RECIDIVISM OVER THREE-YEARS BY 2%.

THE DEPARTMENTS MISSION IS TO MAKE OUR COMMUNITIES SAFER BY REDUCING HARM THROUGH SUPPORTIVE INTERVENTION, EMPOWERING CHANGE, AND RESTORING LIVES. THIS PROJECT WILL ENSURE THAT RESIDENTS RECEIVING OR IN NEED OF MSUD TREATMENT WILL RECEIVE IT WITH DIGNITY AND RESPECT.

NEW ENGLAND ARAB AMERICAN ORGANIZATION (NEAAO), A NON-PROFIT 501C3 ETHNIC-BASED ORGANIZATION, WILL COLLABORATE WITH UNIFIED ASIAN COMMUNITIES AND EQUALITY MAINE TO IMPLEMENT MAKING MAINE A PLACE WITHOUT HATE, A STATE-WIDE EFFORT TO IMPROVE RESPONSE TO HATE CRIME, INCREASE REPORTING, ENHANCE VICTIM SERVICES, AND ESTABLISH HATE CRIME AS A PRIORITY AMONG LAW ENFORCEMENT, JUSTICE SYSTEMS, AND WITHIN OUR COMMUNITIES AND NEIGHBORHOODS.  THROUGH THIS PROJECT PARTNERS WILL ESTABLISH A TASK FORCE AGAINST HATE CRIME THAT BRINGS TOGETHER MAINE'S DIVERSE COMMUNITIES, DISTRICT ATTORNEYS, CIVIL RIGHTS SPECIALISTS AND DETECTIVES, MEMBERS OF THE MAINE ATTORNEY GENERAL'S OFFICE, AND A WIDE VARIETY OF STAKEHOLDERS.  THE PARTNERSHIP OF THE THREE ORGANIZATIONS REFLECTS PRIMARY COMMUNITIES IN MAINE THAT HAVE BEEN TARGETED OVER THE LAST FIVE YEARS, AND WHO ALSO HAVE HISTORIES OF WORKING EFFECTIVELY WITHIN SYSTEMS THAT PROSECUTE HATE-FUELED CRIMES AND INCIDENTS.  

MAKING MAINE A STATE WITHOUT HATE BUILDS ON NEAAO'S CURRENT WORK ADDRESSING HATE CRIME THROUGH A FUTURES WITHOUT VIOLENCE COMMUNITY IMPACT GRANT.  THE BJA GRANT WILL ENABLE NEAAO TO PARTNER WITH COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS TO CONTINUE BUILDING RELATIONSHIPS AMONG DISTRICT ATTORNEYS, THE MAINE ATTORNEY GENERALS OFFICE, AND LAW ENFORCEMENT. TASK FORCE EFFORTS WILL ALSO SUPPORT A MAJOR PUBLIC INFORMATION CAMPAIGN COMPRISED OF PSAS, SOCIAL MEDIA, MUNICIPAL SIGNAGE AND WIDESPREAD OUTREACH TO IMMIGRANT, LGBTQI+ AND BIPOC COMMUNITIES TO ENCOURAGE REPORTING.  BETWEEN 2019 AND 2021, THE NUMBER OF HATE CRIME REPORTS INCREASED FROM 19 TO 83, WITH THE BULK OF CRIMES TARGETING PEOPLE OF COLOR, ASIAN AMERICANS, MUSLIMS AND LGBTQ+ INDIVIDUALS.  MAINE ALSO CONTENDS WITH SOME VERY ACTIVE WHITE SUPREMACY GROUPS, INCLUDING PATRIOT FRONT AND NSC-13.

THE PROJECT TAKES A THREE-PRONG APPROACH TO PREVENTION AND INTERVENTION:  1) BUILD RELATIONSHIPS AND UNDERSTANDINGS THROUGH A MONTHLY TASK FORCE AGAINST HATE CRIME;  2) ENGAGE IN CULTURALLY AND LINGUISTICALLY APPROPRIATE OUTREACH TO TARGETED COMMUNITIES  TO INCREASE REPORTING AND BUILD TRUST; AND 3) DEVELOP A STRONG AND WELL-RESOURCED VICTIM SERVICE NETWORK THAT CAN RESPOND QUICKLY AND ALSO PROMOTE HEALING. 

WHILE MAKING MAINE A STATE WITHOUT HATE INVOLVES THREE MAJOR PARTNERS, THERE ARE MORE THAN 60 ORGANIZATIONS, POLICE DEPARTMENTS, AND JUSTICE PROFESSIONALS WHO WILL BE INVOLVED IN GROWING THE PROGRAM OVER THREE YEARS AND ENSURING SUCCESS.

THE MAINE STATISTICAL ANALYSIS CENTER (SAC), PROPOSES TO IMPLEMENT A CORE CAPACITY-BUILDING PROJECT: INCREASING ACCESS TO MAINE CRIMINAL JUSTICE DATA THROUGH BUILDING A FOUNDATIONAL DATA WAREHOUSE INFRASTRUCTURE. INNOVATIONS IN DATA MANAGEMENT AND ANALYSIS SYSTEMS NOW MAKE IT POSSIBLE TO COLLECT, PROCESS, AND REPORT MAINE CRIMINAL JUSTICE DATA GENERATED BY NUMEROUS STATE AGENCIES IN AN ACCURATE, PROMPT, AND ACCESSIBLE FASHION. HOWEVER, MAINE CRIMINAL JUSTICE DATA ARE HOUSED IN A MULTITUDE OF LOCATIONS AND A SOLE REPOSITORY DOES NOT CURRENTLY EXIST. THEREFORE, THIS PROPOSED ONE-YEAR PROJECT AIMS TO INCREASE ACCESS TO MAINE CRIMINAL JUSTICE DATA BY DEVELOPING A FOUNDATIONAL DATA STORAGE AND MANAGEMENT INFRASTRUCTURE TO DO JUST THAT. THE MAINE SAC SEEKS TO USE STRUCTURED QUERY LANGUAGE SERVER TO CREATE A MAINE SAC DATA WAREHOUSE THAT WILL BE CAPABLE OF STORING, MANIPULATING, AND MANAGING CRIMINAL JUSTICE DATA IN ONE SCALABLE ENVIRONMENT. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE USING NATIONAL INCIDENT-BASED REPORTING SYSTEM DATA AND MAINE PROSECUTORIAL DATA TO BUILD APPROPRIATE TABLES AND SCHEMA THAT WILL BE CAPABLE OF EFFICIENTLY INCORPORATING NEW DATA IMPORTS AND UPDATING EXISTING DATA. ONCE BUILT, THE MAINE SAC DATA WAREHOUSE WILL BE DIRECTLY LINKED TO POWER BI SO THAT CRIMINAL JUSTICE DATA CAN BE EFFECTIVELY VISUALIZED THROUGH TOPIC-SPECIFIC, PUBLIC-FACING DATA DASHBOARDS ON THE MAINE SAC WEBSITE. THIS CAPACITY-BUILDING EFFORT WILL MAKE THE MAINE SAC WELL-POSITIONED FOR FUTURE COLLABORATIONS WITH MAINE CRIMINAL JUSTICE AGENCIES THAT SEEK TO USE INTERACTIVE DATA VISUALIZATIONS FOR COMPLEX DATASETS AND MAKE MEANINGFUL DATA AVAILABLE TO A WIDE AUDIENCE.

THE LONG AND DIVERSE BORDERLINE OF THE U.S. POSES A GREAT CHALLENGE FOR HSE TO MANAGE IT IN AN EFFICIENT WAY. ONE PROMISING DIRECTION TO EXPLORE IS UTILIZATION OF UNMANNED VEHICLES (UVS) TO HELP TO SECURE AND MANAGE THE BORDERS. TO FULLY UNLEASH THE POTENTIAL OF UVS TO IMPROVE THE OPERATION EFFICIENCY ON BORDER SECURITY, IT IS NECESSARY TO LEVERAGE RECENT PROGRESSES IN AI FOR UV CONTROL AND USE DIFFERENT TYPES OF UVS TO FORM A SWARM. THE RESEARCH COMPONENT OF THE PROJECT FOCUSES ON THREE ASPECTS OF BUILDING SUCH SYSTEM FOR HSE TASKS: AI-BASED SWARM CONTROL, GRAPH THEORY FOR FORMATION CONTROL, AND SECURITY OF AI-DRIVEN SWARM, INCLUDING THEIR APPLICATIONS IN COUNTER-DRONE. THE EDUCATION COMPONENT IS INTEGRATED WITH THE RESEARCH TASKS. BY COLLABORATING WITH A WIDE RANGE OF STAKEHOLDERS (DHS COES, INDUSTRY PARTNERS, AND COMMUNITY COLLEGES), THE PROJECT WILL EXPOSE STUDENTS FROM CSUN AND PARTNER COMMUNITY COLLEGES TO CUTTING-EDGE RESEARCHES ON SWARM FOR HS TASKS, AND OBTAINING INTERNSHIPS OPPORTUNITIES. THESE EXPERIENCES HELPS THEM TO PURSUE HIGHER DEGREES AND FINALLY ENHANCE THE DIVERSITY OF HIGH QUALITY HSE WORKFORCE.

grants.description: THE HOMELAND SECURITY ENTERPRISE (HSE) IS FACING A SIGNIFICANT TASK IN DEVELOPING A SKILLED AND DIVERSE WORKFORCE THAT CAN ADDRESS THE COMPLEX AND EVOLVING THREATS TO NATIONAL SECURITY. TO BE READY FOR FUTURE CHALLENGES, HSE REQUIRES A DIVERSE AND COMPETENT WORKFORCE THAT SPECIALIZES IN AREAS SUCH AS COUNTER TERRORISM, BORDER SECURITY, CYBERSECURITY, SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT AND DISASTER MANAGEMENT. THERE IS A PARTICULAR NEED IN THE LOS ANGELES AND SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA REGION, WHERE THE BORDER, MAJOR PORTS (LONG BEACH AND LA) AND INTERNATIONAL AIRPORTS (LAX) PRESENT CRITICAL SECURITY CHALLENGES SUCH AS INTERNATIONAL TRADE AND IMMIGRATION. THE REGION ALSO HAS A HIGH LIKELIHOOD OF EXPERIENCING NATURAL HAZARDS LIKE WILDFIRE, EARTHQUAKE, DROUGHT, HEATWAVES, AND FLOODS, WITH VULNERABLE POPULATIONS AND LOCATIONS ESPECIALLY SUSCEPTIBLE TO THESE DISASTERS. AS A MINORITY SERVING INSTITUTION (MSI) IN THE REGION, CSUDH CAN PLAY A CRITICAL ROLE IN TRAINING A QUALIFIED, MORE DIVERSE HS WORKFORCE BY CREATING EVIDENCE-BASED CAREER PATHWAYS FROM COMMUNITY COLLEGES TO OUR CAMPUS, ON TO USC AND BEYOND, AS WELL AS CONDUCTING STATE-OF-THE-ART RESEARCH ALONGSIDE STUDENTS ON INNOVATIVE SOLUTIONS TO INFORM REGIONAL HSE STAKEHOLDERS.WE PROPOSE LAUNCHING THE HOMELAND SECURITY INITIATIVE AT CALIFORNIA STATE UNIVERSITY, DOMINGUEZ HILLS (CSUDH) TO BUILD OUR UNIVERSITY CAPACITY IN INTERDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH, EDUCATION AND WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT FOR HOMELAND SECURITY ENTERPRISE (HSE) TO SERVE THE LOS ANGELES REGION. THE INITIATIVE HAS THREE MAJOR GOALS: 1) RECRUIT AND SUPPORT STUDENTS TOWARDS COMPLETING SCIENCE, TECHNOLOGY, ENGINEERING, AND MATHEMATICS (STEM) OR HOMELAND SECURITY (HS) RELATED DEGREES THROUGH IMPROVED HS-RELEVANT CURRICULA, EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING AND INTEGRATED RESEARCH  2) BUILD RESEARCH CAPACITY IN HSE TOPICS AT CSUDH THROUGH SUPPORTING INNOVATIVE, INTERDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH PROJECTS AND FUNDING DEVELOPMENT  3) DEVELOP A DIVERSE AND QUALIFIED WORKFORCE THAT IS READY FOR THE FUTURE HS CHALLENGES, ESPECIALLY IN THE LOS ANGELES REGION.       THE FIRST GOAL OF EDUCATIONAL OUTCOMES IS ACHIEVED THROUGH THE FOLLOWING OBJECTIVES: 1) DEVELOPING 4 NEW COURSES FOR HSE THAT ARE DESIGNED TO THE LATEST PEDAGOGICAL STANDARDS, INCORPORATE EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING, AND FACILITATE CULTURAL COMPETENCY  2) UPDATING 17 EXISTING HOMELAND SECURITY-RELATED COURSES IN VARIOUS DEGREE PROGRAMS TO MEET THESE SAME STANDARDS  3) STUDENT RECRUITMENT AT PARTNERING COMMUNITY COLLEGES  4) AWARDING 20 DHS SLA SCHOLARSHIPS OVER FIVE YEARS TO SUPPORT STUDENT LEARNING 5) HOSTING 3 SERIES OF EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING AND TRAINING PROGRAMS.FOR OUR SECOND GOAL OF BUILD RESEARCH CAPACITY IN HSE, WE WILL LAUNCH 1) 14 IMPACTFUL INTERDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH PROJECTS, WHICH COVERS TOPICS INCLUDING CYBERSECURITY, MARITIME SECURITY, SUPPLY CHAIN DISRUPTION, SYSTEM ENGINEERING, DISASTER MANAGEMENT, COUNTERTERRORISM AND SOCIAL MEDIA ANALYTICS  2) INTEGRATION OF STUDENTS AND FACULTY IN PROPOSED RESEARCH PROJECTS WITH 30 STUDENT RAS  3) RESEARCH COLLABORATION WITH DHS COE, USC CENTER FOR RISK AND ECONOMIC ANALYSIS OF THREATS AND EMERGENCIES (CREATE) TO SUPPORT CSUDH STUDENT EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING AND FACULTY DEVELOPMENT  4) INCENTIVES FOR GRANT DEVELOPMENT, CONFERENCE PRESENTATIONS AND OTHER CAPACITY BUILDING ACTIVITIES.THE THIRD GOAL IS WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT WITH A FOCUS IN THE LA REGION. WE WILL DEVELOP: 1) STUDENT INTERNSHIP PROGRAM WITH REGIONAL PARTNERS (TOTAL OF 15 INTERNSHIP STIPENDS)  2) MENTORSHIP PROGRAM  FOR HSE WORKING PROJECTS TO PROVIDE CAREER GUIDANCE TO CSUDH AND LASC STUDENTS  3) CAREER TRAINING AND APPRENTICESHIP OPPORTUNITIES WITH SOUTH BAY WORKFORCE INVESTMENT BOARD (SBWIB) IN AREAS SUCH AS CYBER SECURITY  4) PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT AND NETWORKING EVENTS HELD REGULARLY ON CAMPUS.

THE ALASKA PARTE (PROGRAM FOR ARCTIC RESEARCH, TRAINING AND EDUCATION) SERVES TO GREATLY ASSIST THE RESEARCH-BASED EDUCATION INTERNSHIP PROGRAMS THAT EXIST WITHIN THE UNIVERSITY OF ALASKAS (UA), ARCTIC DOMAIN AWARENESS CENTER (ADAC) AND APPLIED ENVIRONMENTAL RESEARCH CENTER (AERC). THESE CENTERS SHARE A MISSION THAT ENCOMPASS PROGRAMS DESIGNATED FOR CAREER DEVELOPMENT OPPORTUNITIES AND DIRECTLY ENGAGE WITH UA COMMUNITY CAMPUSES AND CAREER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION PROGRAMS. ADDITIONALLY, THE EXPECTATION FOR STUDENTS INCLUDES FILLING ESSENTIAL ROLES IN RESEARCH PROJECTS THAT SUPPORT THE DEPARTMENT OF HOMELAND SECURITY (DHS) AND DEPARTMENT OF DEFENSE (DOD) MISSIONS WHILE ENGAGING STUDENTS IN STEM RELATED ACTIVITIES AND RELATED DISCIPLINES.IN 2022, THE UNIVERSITY OF ALASKA ANCHORAGE, APPLIED ENVIRONMENTAL RESEARCH CENTER (AERC) AND ARCTIC DOMAIN AWARENESS CENTER (ADAC) INTEGRATED THEIR STUDENT FELLOWSHIP PROGRAMS TO ENHANCE EDUCATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES AND SERVE A GREATER NUMBER OF STUDENTS INCLUDING TARGETING UNDERREPRESENTED CLASSES. WHILE BOTH AERC AND ADAC ARE HOUSED AT THE UNIVERSITY OF ALASKA ANCHORAGE, THEY SUPPORT THE ENTIRE UNIVERSITY OF ALASKA (UA) SYSTEM. THE AERC OPERATES ONE OF THE FIRST FEDERALLY AUTHORIZED REGISTERED APPRENTICESHIP TRAINING PROGRAMS FOR RESEARCHERS APPROVED BY THE US DEPARTMENT OF LABOR. MERGING THIS STUDENT SUCCESS INITIATIVE WITH ADACS WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, FELLOWSHIP AND ARCTIC SUMMER INTERNSHIP PROGRAM PROVIDES A CENTRALIZED UNIT UNDER THE UNIVERSITY OF ALASKA SYSTEM DESIGNATED TO SUPPORT OUR FEDERAL PARTNERS AND SIGNIFICANTLY CONTRIBUTE TO THE UNIVERSITYS MISSION OF TRANSFORMING LIVES THROUGH TEACHING, RESEARCH, COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT AND CREATIVE EXPRESSION IN A DIVERSE AND INCLUSIVE ENVIRONMENT. ALASKAS PARTE WILL PROVIDE OPPORTUNITIES FOR STUDENTS TO ASSIST THE DHS AND DOD MISSIONS BY ACTIVELY ENGAGING STUDENTS IN RESEARCH PROJECTS ASSOCIATED WITH: ADVANCED DATA ANALYSIS AND VISUALIZATION  ENVIRONMENTAL CHALLENGES ASSOCIATED WITH CLIMATE CHANGE  COMMUNICATIONS AND INTEROPERABILITY  COMMUNITY (TO INCLUDE ALASKA NATIVE AND RURAL PROBLEMS AND CONCERNS)  COMMERCE  INFRASTRUCTURE RESILIENCE  EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS AND RESPONSE  MARITIME AND PORT SECURITY  NATURAL DISASTERS AND RELATED GEOPHYSICAL STUDIES  SEARCH AND RESCUE  ARCTIC DOMAIN AWARENESS  BORDER SECURITY  AND DECISION SCIENCES. THE AERC ADAC HAS BEEN PROACTIVE AT ASSISTING EDUCATIONALLY DISADVANTAGED AND UNDERREPRESENTED POPULATIONS IN POSTSECONDARY EDUCATION AS WELL AS MINORITY STUDENTS WITH ASSOCIATE, BACHELORS AND OR ADVANCED DEGREES FOR ALMOST A DECADE. BOTH OF THE CENTERS WERE ESTABLISHED IN 2014, THE ARCTIC DOMAIN AWARENESS CENTER (ADAC) IS RECOGNIZED AS A CENTER OF EXCELLENCE (COE) IN MARITIME RESEARCH BY DHS AND BRINGS A WEALTH OF KNOWLEDGE TO SUPPORT STUDENT SUCCESS INITIATIVES. THE AERC CONSISTS OF A DIVERSE NETWORK OF ARCTIC SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY ACADEMICS AND CURRENTLY HAS MORE THAN A DOZEN PROJECTS FUNDED BY THE UNITED STATES ARMY CORPS OF ENGINEERS AND PROVIDES PATHWAYS FOR STUDENTS TO PARTICIPATE IN NUMEROUS DOD FUNDED PROJECTS PERTAINING TO ENVIRONMENTAL CONSERVATION AND CLIMATE CHANGE RELATED RESEARCH. BOTH CENTERS HOST STRONG ORGANIZATIONAL AND FISCAL LEADERS AND ADMINISTRATORS THAT SERVE TO CREATE ENRICHING OPPORTUNITIES FOR STUDENTS WHILE BUILDING THE NEXT GENERATION OF GOVERNMENT LEADERS AND SCIENTISTS.

THIS PROJECT AIMS TO PROVIDE SOUTH TEXAS STUDENTS IN THE COASTAL BEND REGION AS WELL AS INDUSTRY PROFESSIONALS, OPPORTUNITIES IN CYBER INTELLIGENCE EDUCATION. THE PROJECT WILL DEVELOP INTENSIVE ACCELERATED TRAINING IN CYBER INTELLIGENCE (IAT-CI) FOR HIGH SCHOOL, COMMUNITY COLLEGE, AND UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS AT THE FRESHMAN AND SOPHOMORE LEVELS. TO REACH BROADER AUDIENCES, THE PROGRAM WILL DEVELOP AN ONLINE CERTIFICATE PROGRAM IN CYBER INTELLIGENCE (OCP-CI) THAT ATTRACTS INDUSTRY PROFESSIONALS. THIS WILL GIVE TEXAS A M UNIVERSITY-KINGSVILLE (TAMUK) THE VISIBILITY AND THE CAPABILITY TO PREPARE AND CREDENTIAL PROFESSIONALS TO JOIN THE DEPARTMENT OF HOMELAND SECURITY (DHS) WORKFORCE BY PROVIDING CYBER INTELLIGENCE EDUCATION, TRAINING, RESEARCH EXPERIENCES, AWARENESS, AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT. ADDITIONALLY, THIS PROJECT AIMS TO INCREASE THE INVOLVEMENT AND NUMBER OF MARGINALIZED UNDERREPRESENTED MINORITIES AVAILABLE AND QUALIFIED TO CONTRIBUTE TO THE DHS WORKFORCE IN THE FIELD OF CYBER INTELLIGENCE. THIS MULTI-TIERED EDUCATION IN CYBER INTELLIGENCE WILL BE OFFERED BY THE COMPUTER SCIENCE FACULTY AT TAMUK. THE IAT-CI AND OCP-CI PROGRAMS WILL BE OPEN TO ALL STEM AND NON-STEM FIELDS. THE EXISTING PARTNERSHIP WITH THE DHS CBTS COE AT TEXAS A M UNIVERSITY COLLEGE STATION (TAMU) WILL BE LEVERAGED TO MENTOR THE CURRICULUM DEVELOPMENT PROCESS FOR THE IAT-CI AND OCP-CI PROGRAMS. THE NEW PARTNERSHIPS WITH DHS CINA COE AT GEORGE MASON UNIVERSITY (MSU) AND LOUISIANA STATE UNIVERSITY (LSU) CAE-CO WILL GROW THE EXPERTISE IN THE CYBER INTELLIGENCE IN THIS PROGRAM. EARLY-CAREER AND RESEARCH FACULTY AND SELECTED STUDENTS FROM TAMUK WILL PARTICIPATE IN CBTSS SUMMER RESEARCH PROGRAM.MOREOVER, THE EARLY-CAREER AND RESEARCH FACULTY WILL DEVELOP A WORLD-CLASS RESEARCH PROGRAM IN AI-BASED CYBER INTELLIGENCE LEVERAGING THE COLLABORATIONS WITH CBTS COE AT TAMU, LSU CENTER OF ACADEMIC EXCELLENCE IN CYBER OPERATIONS (CAE-CO), TEXAS A M UNIVERSITY-SAN ANTONIO, UNIVERSITY OF NORTH TEXAS, AND XAVIER UNIVERSITY OF LOUISIANA. EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING OPPORTUNITIES WITH FINANCIAL SUPPORT WILL BE PROVIDED TO ELIGIBLE AND QUALIFIED TAMUK STUDENTS WHO HAVE ALREADY COMPLETED THE IAT-CI TRAINING AND ARE PURSUING A COMPUTER SCIENCE DEGREE OR THE MINOR OR CERTIFICATE PROGRAMS IN CYBER INTELLIGENCE. THE FUNDED POSITIONS WILL INCLUDE SUMMER RESEARCH ASSISTANTSHIPS, FELLOWSHIPS, AND INTERNSHIPS AT TAMU CBTS COE, LSU CAE-CO, NATIONAL LABS, AND PRIVATE INDUSTRIES. MOREOVER, THE PROJECT WILL ESTABLISH A CYBER INTELLIGENCE RESEARCH LAB (CIRL) TO FACILITATE THE PLANNED TRAINING, ONLINE CERTIFICATION, AND UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE RESEARCH IN CYBER INTELLIGENCE. THE EARLY CAREER AND RESEARCH FACULTY WILL LEAD CYBER INTELLIGENCE RESEARCH PROJECTS USING THE CIRL LAB.

THERE IS A DEARTH OF STUDENTS, AND PARTICULARLY OF MINORITIZED STUDENTS (E.G., THOSE WHO IDENTIFY AS WOMEN, BLACK OR AFRICAN AMERICAN, AND OR HISPANIC OR LATINX) IN COMPUTING, AND ESPECIALLY THOSE WHO ARE QUALIFIED FOR PROFESSIONS IN HOMELAND SECURITY ENTERPRISE (HSE). TO BROADEN PARTICIPATION  ENHANCE EDUCATION, RESEARCH, AND WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT IN THE HOMELAND SECURITY SCIENCE, TECHNOLOGY, ENGINEERING, AND MATHEMATICS (HS-STEM) AREAS  AND BUILD CAPACITY FOR COLLEGE STUDENTS, UNIVERSITY STUDENTS, AND FACULTY TO MAKE CONNECTIONS WITH HSE, FLORIDA INTERNATIONAL UNIVERSITY (FIU) PROPOSES THE CREATION OF THE ADVANCED EDUCATION AND RESEARCH FOR MACHINE LEARNING-DRIVEN CRITICAL INFRASTRUCTURE RESILIENCE (ADMIRE) CENTER. THE ADMIRE CENTER IS EXPECTED TO PROVIDE AN INTEGRATED RESEARCH AND EDUCATION FRAMEWORK WITH A SPECIAL FOCUS ON THREE OF THE DHS OPERATIONAL TOPICS OF INTEREST, I.E., CRITICAL INFRASTRUCTURE RESILIENCE, CYBERSECURITY, AND MACHINE LEARNING (ML). THE CENTER BENEFITS FROM COLLABORATIONS WITH MIAMI DADE COLLEGE (MDC), THREE DHS CENTERS OF EXCELLENCE (COE), AND OTHER HSE PARTNERS TO ENRICH THE PROPOSED EDUCATION AND RESEARCH ACTIVITIES FOR FIU AND MDC STUDENTS, AS WELL AS FACULTY. THE PROJECT WILL INVOLVE A TEAM OF SEVEN HIGHLY PRODUCTIVE FACULTY MEMBERS (FOUR OF WHOM ARE EARLY CAREER FACULTY) AT FIUS KNIGHT FOUNDATION SCHOOL OF COMPUTING AND INFORMATION SCIENCES AND THE SCHOOL OF UNIVERSAL COMPUTING, CONSTRUCTION, AND ENGINEERING EDUCATION, WHO HAVE STRONG EXPERTISE IN HS-STEM TOPICS, AS WELL AS COMPUTING AND ENGINEERING EDUCATION AND RESEARCH. IN ORDER TO EDUCATE, TRAIN, AND MENTOR STUDENTS AND EARLY CAREER FACULTY, THE CENTER WILL CONDUCT THE FOLLOWING EDUCATION AND RESEARCH ACTIVITIES: (1) THE CENTER WILL PROVIDE SCHOLARSHIPS TO CREATE A SUSTAINABLE PIPELINE FOR 2-YEAR MDC STUDENTS TO TRANSITION TO FIU, AS WELL AS OFFERING SCHOLARSHIPS TO FIU UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE STUDENTS SPECIALIZED IN HS-STEM AREAS TO PREPARE THEM FOR HSE CAREERS, PROVIDE THEM WITH EDUCATION, MENTORING, AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT RESOURCES, ASSIST THEM WITH INTERNSHIP AND CAREER PLACEMENT AT RESEARCH AND GOVERNMENT LABS, AND AT OUR PARTNER DHS COES  (2) THE CENTER WILL DEVELOP AND INTEGRATE HS-STEM TEACHING MODULES AND RESEARCH OUTCOMES IN EXISTING COMPUTER SCIENCE, INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY, CYBERSECURITY, DATA SCIENCE, AND ENGINEERING COURSES AT FIU, AND DEVELOP NEW COURSES TO EXPLORE INNOVATIVE AREAS OF DEPLOYING ML FOR CRITICAL INFRASTRUCTURE RESILIENCE AND SECURITY  (3) STRONG TEAMS OF RESEARCHERS WILL CONDUCT INNOVATIVE RESEARCH PROJECTS IN IMPORTANT AREAS OF CRITICAL INFRASTRUCTURE RESILIENCE AND SECURITY USING ADVANCED ML TECHNIQUES  (4) THE CENTER WILL BUILD CAPACITY FOR RESEARCH AND EDUCATION ON HS-STEM TOPICS BY ENGAGING EARLY CAREER FACULTY WITH THE SUPPORT MENTORSHIP FROM SENIOR FACULTY PARTICIPANTS, EACH WITH PRIOR ENGAGEMENT WITH DHS, AND IN COLLABORATION WITH THREE DHS COES AND OTHER HSE PARTNERS  (5) THE CENTERS RESEARCH OUTCOMES WILL ENLIST TECHNOLOGY TRANSFER ACTIVITIES FOR HSE SUPPORTED BY STARTUP FIU AND OUR INDUSTRY PARTNERS AND THE EDUCATION AND RESEARCH OUTCOMES WILL BE DISSEMINATED TO OTHER INSTITUTIONS FOR INTEGRATION IN THEIR CURRICULUM AND ENSURE SCALABILITY OF OUR HS-STEM EDUCATION EFFORTS.THE CENTER WILL PARTNER WITH THREE DHS COES. THE CENTERS ACTIVITIES ALIGN WELL WITH THE COES GOALS ON HS-STEM EDUCATION, TRAINING, AND WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT AND WILL PROVIDE RESOURCES FOR PROMOTING THE ACTIVE INVOLVEMENT OF MINORITIZED GROUPS IN THESE COES. WE HAVE DEVELOPED AND DEFINED QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE EVALUATION METRICS TO MONITOR AND EVALUATE THE PROGRAM AND ITS IMPACT ON CAPACITY BUILDING FOR FIU AND MDC, AND SHARE THE PERFORMANCE METRICS WITH THE DHS AND OUR EXTERNAL ADVISORY BOARD FOR EVALUATION AND FEEDBACK. INDEPENDENT EVALUATION WILL ALSO BE PERFORMED PERIODICALLY TO ENSURE PROGRAMMATIC ALIGNMENT WITH DHS GOALS.

THE DHC-CREST CENTER AT NCCU AIMS TO ADVANCE INSTITUTIONAL RESEARCH AND EDUCATIONAL CAPABILITIES IN STEM DISCIPLINES RELATED TO DHS AT NCCU AND STRENGTHEN THE PIPELINE FOR THE ADVANCEMENT OF UNDERREPRESENTED MINORITIES IN DHS STEM DISCIPLINES. THIS WILL BE DONE IN PARTNERSHIP WITH THE SENTRY COE AND WILL LEVERAGE THE ASSETS OF BOTH INSTITUTIONS TO ENABLE SIGNIFICANT INCREASES IN MINORITY PARTICIPATION IN MATERIAL SCIENCE AND AT THE SAME TIME PRODUCE RESEARCH AND EDUCATIONAL OUTCOMES THAT HAVE A SIGNIFICANT IMPACT BEYOND THE TIME LIMITS OF THIS FUNDING. THE VISION OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO ESTABLISH NCCU AS A PREMIER INSTITUTION IN DHS DETECTOR SCIENCE WITH THE ACCOMPANYING INFRASTRUCTURE AND HUMAN CAPITAL NECESSARY FOR SUCH A TRANSFORMATION. THE RESEARCH THRUST AT THE CORE OF THIS PROPOSAL IS HIGH SELECTIVITY AND HIGH SENSITIVITY LABEL FREE BIOCHEMICAL SENSOR FOR CONTINUING DETECTION BASED ON QUANTUM CONFINEMENT. THE DETECTION PRINCIPLE ALLOWS FOR CONTINUOUS MONITORING WITHOUT DETECTOR REFRESHING, WHICH COULD BE A SIGNIFICANT CONTRIBUTION TO DHS. THE DETECTOR IS IN MANY WAYS SIMILAR TO THE SENTRY DETECTOR, WHICH CONTINUOUSLY DETECTS TRACES OF TRIACETONE TRIPEROXIDE OR TATP. THAT WILL ALLOW OUR TEAM TO GET VALUABLE EXPERIENCE WORKING FIRST ON THE ELEMENTS OF THE SENTRY DETECTOR AND LATER INCORPORATING OUR DETECTOR INTO THE SENTRY PLATFORM. THE PROPOSED PARTNERSHIP ADDRESSES A KEY EDUCATIONAL CHALLENGE MANIFESTED IN THE LOW PARTICIPATION OF UNDERREPRESENTED MINORITIES IN MATERIAL SCIENCE. THE VISION IS NOT MERELY TO PROVIDE OPPORTUNITIES FOR NCCU STUDENTS TO PARTICIPATE IN THE SENTRY PROGRAM AND THEREBY CORRECT SUCH A DISPARITY. THE INTELLECTUAL MERIT OF THIS PROPOSAL LIES IN THE QUALITY OF THE OPPORTUNITIES PROVIDED AND THE OUTCOMES THAT WILL RESULT. THE FOUR-TIERED PLAN CONSISTS OF A) RECRUITMENT STRATEGIES TARGETED AT THE BEST AND BRIGHTEST HIGH SCHOOL AND COMMUNITY COLLEGE TRANSFER STUDENTS IN THE REGION BY HIGHLIGHTING THE CENTRAL ROLE OF DHS STEM SCIENCE IN THE 21ST CENTURY, B) ACADEMIC ENRICHMENT PROGRAMS FOCUSED ON DHS STEM SCIENCE, C) EFFECTIVE MENTORING PROGRAM WHICH WILL PAIR MINORITY PARTICIPANTS IN THE NCCU WITH MENTORS AT SENTRY AND NCCU, AND D) PRODUCTIVE RESEARCH EXPERIENCES AT THE FRONTIERS OF DHS-STEM SCIENCE SUPPORTED BY CLOSE MENTORING BY BOTH NCCU AND SENTRY FACULTY AND RESEARCHERS AT ALL LEVELS.   THE UNDERLYING FRAMEWORK THAT WILL ENABLE PRODUCTIVE RESEARCH IS THE BROAD AND DEEP LINKS BETWEEN THE INDIVIDUAL RESEARCH THRUSTS AND ONGOING PROJECTS IN THE SENTRY. THESE LINKS WILL LEVERAGE THE EXPERTISE AND RESOURCES IN THE SENTRY TO GENERATE IMPORTANT SCIENTIFIC ADVANCES IN THE SHORT TERM AS WELL AS CREATE SUSTAINABLE RESEARCH PROGRAMS AT NCCU IN THESE AREAS AT THE END OF FIVE YEARS.   THE KEY SCIENTIFIC CHALLENGE THAT IS ADDRESSED IN THIS PROPOSAL IS THE ABILITY TO CONTROL TUNNELING BETWEEN A TARGETED ANALYTE AND DETECTOR NANOSTRUCTURE AND TO USE THAT PHENOMENON FOR ANALYTE DETECTION. MANY TECHNICAL PROBLEMS MUST BE SOLVED TO ACHIEVE THAT GOAL, WHICH WILL EXPOSE STUDENTS AND FACULTY TO FIELDS OF ELECTRONICS, DATA ACQUISITION SYSTEMS, MACHINE LEARNING, ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, COMPUTER SIMULATIONS, AND MAKING ALGORITHMS, AND SOFTWARE FOR DATA ANALYSIS AND DISPLAY OF DATA. THE FACILITIES AND EXPERTISE AVAILABLE VIA OUR PARTNERS AT SENTRY WOULD BE CRITICAL FOR US HERE AT NCCU TO BE ABLE TO TRANSITION TO A LEVEL WHERE THESE ACHIEVEMENTS CAN BE UTILIZED IN ACTUAL DEVICES.          THE PROJECT WILL CREATE A MULTIDISCIPLINARY DHS SCIENCE COMMUNITY AT NCCU THAT WILL INCREASE PUBLIC AWARENESS OF THE FIELD, RECRUIT TALENTED MINORITY STUDENTS TO THIS FIELD, PREPARE THESE STUDENTS FOR FUTURE CAREERS IN THE FIELD THROUGH COMPREHENSIVE ACADEMIC AND RESEARCH PROGRAMS, AND INCREASE RATES OF MATRICULATION OF MINORITY STUDENTS FROM NCCU TO DHS SCIENCE DOCTORAL PROGRAMS AT SENTRY AND ELSEWHERE. THIS PARTNERSHIP WILL ENABLE US TO ATTAIN A HIGHER LEVEL OF RESEARCH CAPABILITY, ENABLING US TO SUSTAIN A NATIONAL REPUTATION.

THIS PROJECT WILL SUPPORT MULTI-YEAR EFFORTS TO DEVELOP A SUSTAINABLE COMPUTER SCIENCE EDUCATION AND CUTTING-EDGE RESEARCH PROGRAM, AND ENHANCE COLLABORATIONS WITH THE HOMELAND SECURITY ENTERPRISE (HSE), AND PREPARE UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS TO FIND A STEM CAREER IN HSE DOMAIN AND ALSO TO SURVIVE THE RIGORS OF GRADUATE STUDIES, AND INCREASE THE DIVERSITY IN THE HSE COMMUNITY, AND PROVIDE CREATIVE LEADERSHIP IN DEVELOPING PATHWAYS TO BREAKTHROUGHS IN THE DOMAIN OF DISASTER RESILIENCE AND NATURAL HAZARDS RESEARCH. THIS COLLABORATIVE PROJECT BETWEEN JOHNSON C. SMITH UNIVERSITY (JCSU) AND STANLY COMMUNITY COLLEGE (SCC) WILL DEVELOP A CULTURE OF LEADING-EDGE INNOVATIVE RESEARCH ENVIRONMENT AND TRAIN UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS WITH RELEVANT EXPERTISE THROUGH EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING   HANDS-ON EXPERIENCE SO AS TO PREPARE STUDENTS TO BE READY FOR CAREERS IN HSE DOMAIN AND GRADUATE SCHOOL IN STEM. THE NEED FOR COMPUTER SCIENCE PROFESSIONALS AND GRADUATES TO FILL THESE NEW JOBS, AND THE REQUISITE TRAINING AND CODING LITERACY, HAS BECOME A MATTER OF NATIONAL IMPORTANCE. THERE ARE MANY PUBLIC STUDIES WHICH ALSO SUGGESTED THAT EDUCATION PROGRAMS COULD BETTER PREPARE STUDENTS FOR A COMPUTER SCIENCE BASED HSE STEM CAREER BY PROVIDING MORE HANDS-ON EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING OPPORTUNITIES  INTEGRATING THEORETICAL AND INDUSTRY-STANDARD THEMES IN THE CURRICULUM  AND PROVIDING BETTER CAREER DEVELOPMENT SUPPORT. THE PROPOSED PROGRAM SEEKS TO BRIDGE THE GAP BETWEEN COMPUTER SCIENCE EDUCATION, ENHANCING THE RESEARCH CAPABILITY AND THE WORKFORCE PREPARATION, BY OFFERING ACADEMIC AND RESEARCH SOLUTIONS GEARED TOWARD MEETING CURRENT AND FUTURE MARKET DEMANDS. THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL BE LED BY FACULTIES FROM JCSU AND SCC WITH VARIOUS RESPONSIBILITIES INCLUDING OVERSEEING FACULTY AND STUDENTS IN RELATIONS TO BUILDING RELATIONS, WHILE ENGAGING ACTIVITIES INVOLVING OTHER EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS, PROGRAM ENTITIES, AS WELL INTERNAL INTERACTIONS WITHIN THE UNIVERSITY. THE PI, CO-PI AND THE PROJECT TEAM WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR DEVELOPING CURRICULUM AND RESEARCH PROJECTS, MANAGING STUDENTS ACTIVITIES, AND COLLECTING PROGRAM DATA.

THE PROJECT S FUNDING WILL BE USED FOR CYBERSECURITY RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT FOR UNDERREPRESENTED UNDERGRADUATES AND EARLY-CAREER FACULTY MEMBERS  AS WELL AS THE CREATION OF CYBERSECURITY EDUCATION PATHWAYS FOR COMMUNITY COLLEGES AND CERTIFICATE PROGRAMS TO ENHANCE CYBERSECURITY SKILLS. THE PROJECT WILL ALSO PROVIDE SUMMER RESEARCH OPPORTUNITIES FOR UNDERGRADUATES IN AREAS SUCH AS CYBER-ETHICS, PRIVACY, TRUST AND FRAUD INVESTIGATION, BLOCKCHAIN, CYBER DATAMINING AND MACHINE LEARNING, AND WEB APPLICATION AND GAME DEVELOPMENT. FACULTY, INCLUDING EARLY CAREER JUNIOR MEMBERS, WILL RESEARCH CYBER DATA ANALYTICS, MACHINE LEARNING (ML), ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI), MALWARE ANALYSIS, SOFTWARE ASSURANCE, AND MOBILITY WITH CRITICAL CYBERINFRASTRUCTURES INCLUDING ENERGY, AGRICULTURE, AND HEALTHCARE SERVICES. THE RESEARCH TEAM WILL DEVELOP NOVEL SOFTWARE TOOLS WITH ALGORITHMS, PROTOTYPES, MODELS, AND MAINTENANCE. THE TEAM WILL ALSO DESIGN MODERN CYBERSECURITY COURSES AND CERTIFICATE PROGRAM FOR ALL STEM STUDENTS IN THE DEPARTMENT OF INFORMATION SCIENCE. THE RESEARCH TEAM WILL CREATE A PATHWAY FOR COMMUNITY COLLEGE STUDENTS TO TRANSFER TO THE FOUR-YEAR PROGRAM AT UNT--PROVIDING OPPORTUNITIES FOR RE-SKILLING OR UP-SKILLING TOWARDS CYBERSECURITY CAREERS AFTER COMPLETING AN ASSOCIATE DEGREE AT THEIR COMMUNITY COLLEGE.

JOBS IN STEM ARE SOME OF THE FASTEST GROWING IN THE WORKFORCE, YET MINORITIES REMAIN UNDERREPRESENTED IN THESE JOBS AT A NATIONAL LEVEL, PARTICULARLY IN THE FIELD OF HOMELAND SECURITY (HS). FIU, WITH COLLABORATIONS FROM MIAMI DADE COLLEGE, GEORGE MASON UNIVERSITYS DHS CENTER OF EXCELLENCE CRIMINAL INVESTIGATIONS AND NETWORK ANALYSIS (DHS COE CINA), AS WELL AS ADDITIONAL HS RESEARCH ENTITIES, WILL ADDRESS THIS PROBLEM BY ENGAGING DIVERSE STUDENTS AND FACULTY IN RESEARCH AND GRADUATE AND UNDERGRADUATE-LEVEL CURRICULA THAT WILL SUPPORT THE HOMELAND SECURITY ENTERPRISE (HSE). FLORIDA INTERNATIONAL UNIVERSITY (FIU) IS A MULTI-CAMPUS PUBLIC RESEARCH UNIVERSITY OFFERING A BROAD ARRAY OF UNDERGRADUATE, GRADUATE, AND PROFESSIONAL PROGRAMS. AS A MINORITY-SERVING INSTITUTION (MSI), 85  OF FIU STUDENTS ARE HISPANIC, BLACK, ASIAN OR PACIFIC ISLANDER, OR OTHER MINORITY GROUPS. FIU IS ALSO RANKED R1 (DOCTORAL UNIVERSITIES  VERY HIGH RESEARCH ACTIVITY), THE HIGHEST LEVEL AWARDED IN THE CARNEGIE CLASSIFICATION OF INSTITUTIONS OF HIGHER EDUCATION. AS THE LARGEST PRODUCER OF STEM DEGREES FOR HISPANICS IN THE US, FIU HAS ESTABLISHED ITSELF AS A LEADING MSI WORKING TO ADVANCE DIVERSITY IN STEM. THROUGH ITS TWO PREEMINENT PROGRAMS, THE GLOBAL FORENSIC JUSTICE CENTER (GFJC) AND THE STEM TRANSFORMATION INSTITUTE (STEM TI), FIU PROPOSES THE TRANSFORMING FORENSIC CHEMISTRY EDUCATION AND RESEARCH TO SERVE THE HOMELAND SECURITY ENTERPRISE AND ESTABLISH A DIVERSE WORKFORCE PROGRAM. THROUGH THIS ROBUST PROGRAM, FIU WILL CONDUCT RESEARCH TO IMPROVE DETECTION OF CONCEALED THREATS BY INSTRUMENTS AND CANINE, BROADEN THE REACH OF OUR ESTABLISHED FORENSIC PROGRAM TO INCLUDE HS TOPICS, AND CREATE AN EDUCATIONAL ENVIRONMENT TO ENCOURAGE MINORITY PARTICIPATION IN STEM AND HS-RELATED RESEARCH NEEDS. OUR TEAM PROPOSES TO STRENGTHEN DHS APPROACHES STRATEGICALLY AND SCIENTIFICALLY IN BORDER SECURITY, COUNTERING BIOTHREATS IN SUPPLY CHAINS, LAW ENFORCEMENT INVESTIGATIONS, TRANSPORTATION SECURITY AND SCREENING, AND TERRORISM PREVENTION. CO-DIRECTED BY GFJCS PROFESSOR OF FORENSIC CHEMISTRY, DR. LAURYN DEGREEFF, AND STEM TIS PROFESSOR OF CHEMISTRY EDUCATION RESEARCH, DR. JUSTIN CARMEL, THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL SERVE THE MISSION OF DHS AT THE HIGHEST LEVELS. THE OBJECTIVES OF FIUS SCIENTIFIC LEADERSHIP AWARD PROPOSAL ARE TO 1) PROVIDE RESEARCH OPPORTUNITIES FOR UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE STUDENTS AND FACULTY IN AREAS RELATING TO HS WITH A FOCUS ON PREVENTION OF TERRORISM AND SECURING OUR BORDERS THROUGH VARIOUS METHODS OF THREAT DETECTION  2) RETHINK TRADITIONAL COURSEWORK TO INCLUDE EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING ACTIVITIES FOR STUDENTS AT ALL POST-SECONDARY LEVELS IN ORDER TO PREPARE THEM FOR CAREERS IN THE FIELD OF HS, 3) ENGAGE WITH MIAMI DADE COLLEGE TO BRING CAREER-RELEVANT INFORMATION TO THEIR DOORSTEP AND PROMOTE PATHWAYS TOWARD STEM DEGREE COMPLETION AND TRANSITION FROM 2-YEAR TO 4-YEAR INSTITUTIONS, AND 4) ENGAGE WITH DHS COE CINA AND ADDITIONAL HSE RESEARCH COLLABORATORS TO ENSURE THE PROGRAM EFFECTIVELY SUPPORTS THE HSE. OUR VISION IS THAT THESE AREAS OF RESEARCH AND WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT WILL BRING FURTHER ALIGNMENT OF PRACTICES AND CAPABILITIES TO MAKE IMMEDIATE, NOTABLE, AND MEASURABLE IMPACTS TO DETECT AND DETER TERRORISM AND INCREASE SECURITY FOR ALL OUR CITIZENS, AS WELL AS BUILD A PREPARED, KNOWLEDGEABLE, AND DIVERSE WORKFORCE FOR THE HSE.

AS THE CENTER OF EXCELLENCE FOR HOMELAND SECURITY IN THE ARCTIC, THE ARCTIC DOMAIN AWARENESS CENTER (ADAC) WILL ADDRESS CHALLENGES ACROSS THE HOMELAND SECURITY ENTERPRISE (HSE), ADDING ARCTIC TO ITS NAME TO REPRESENT ITS EXPANDED STRATEGIC VISION. ADACARCTIC WILL DRAW ON ITS EXPERIENCE OPERATING THE PREVIOUS DEPARTMENT OF HOMELAND SECURITY (DHS) ARCTIC REGIONAL CENTER TO CREATE AN INTERDISCIPLINARY NEXUS OF STRATEGIC LEADERS AND PARTNERS CAPABLE OF APPLYING EXPERTISE THROUGHOUT THE HSE. GUIDED BY ITS TEAM OF EXPERT RESEARCHERS, EDUCATORS, WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT PROFESSIONALS, TRANSFER AND TRANSITION EXPERTS, AND COMMUNITY PARTNERS, ADACARCTIC IS READY TO RESPOND TO THE CHALLENGES CONFRONTING DHS IN THE RAPIDLY CHANGING ARCTIC DOMAIN. IT WILL DO SO BY BRINGING TOGETHER AN ARRAY OF GEOGRAPHICALLY DISPERSED, STRATEGICALLY SELECTED PARTNERS FROM ACADEMIA, FEDERALLY-FUNDED RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT CENTERS, INDUSTRY, NON-PROFITS, TRIBAL, AND OTHER FEDERAL, STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS WITH ARCTIC EXPERTISE. THROUGH THESE PARTNERSHIPS, ADACARCTIC WILL STIMULATE INNOVATIVE RESEARCH IDEAS AND PROJECTS, EXPAND WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT AND EDUCATIONAL ACTIVITIES, AND PROMOTE CENTER ENGAGEMENTS THAT PRODUCE TOOLS, TECHNOLOGIES, KNOWLEDGE PRODUCTS, AND TRAINED PERSONNEL. EACH PROJECT AND ACTIVITY WILL INVOLVE STUDENTS OR TRAINEES WHILE YIELDING A PRODUCT FOR TRANSFER AND TRANSITION, ALL TO EMPOWER HSE PERSONNEL AND SERVE THE DHS MISSION. ADACARCTICS SELECTED RESEARCH AND EDUCATION PROJECTS WILL CREATE STATE-OF-THE-ART TECHNOLOGIES TO FILL KNOWLEDGE GAPS AND SOLVE THE TOUGHEST CHALLENGES IN THE ARCTIC. THE SELECTED PROJECTS AIM TO TRANSITION TECHNOLOGY PRODUCTS THAT INCLUDE BUOYS AND DRONES TO MONITOR ENVIRONMENTAL CHANGE FROM CHRONIC OR ACUTE CHANGES DISASTERS, TOOLS SUCH AS RISK ASSESSMENT EVALUATION METHODS FOR INFRASTRUCTURE AND METHODOLOGIES TO IMPROVE DECISION MAKING FOR RISK EVALUATORS AND RESPONDERS, MODELS FOR FAILED OIL WELL MANAGEMENT AND THE INTEGRATION OF A DIVERSE ENERGY PORTFOLIO, AND KNOWLEDGE PRODUCTS SUCH AS REFEREED PUBLICATIONS, LITERATURE REVIEWS, FEASIBILITY STUDIES, AND RAPPORT REPORTS. EDUCATIONAL, WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, AND COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT PROGRAMS INCLUDE AN INTEGRATED MULTI-INSTITUTION INTERDISCIPLINARY ARCTIC SECURITY GRADUATE DEGREE, A CENTER-LED ADACARCTIC STUDENT FELLOWSHIP PROGRAM INCORPORATING FELLOWS ON ACTIVE PROJECTS, TRIBAL ENGAGEMENT AND LIAISING, AND TRAINING PROGRAMS CREATED TO MEET SPECIFIC HSE NEEDS. THE KNOWLEDGE PRODUCTS WILL BE DISSEMINATED INTO THE SCIENTIFIC LITERATURE AND HSE THROUGH PAPERS, PRESENTATIONS, VIDEOS, AND WORKSHOPS COORDINATED AND PROMOTED BY THE CENTER. THE TECHNOLOGY PRODUCTS WILL BE TRANSFERRED AND TRANSITIONED TO DHS COMPONENTS AND INDUSTRIAL PARTNERS IN CLOSE COLLABORATION WITH THE UAA TECHNOLOGY TRANSFER OFFICE (TTO). MOREOVER, ADACARCTIC WILL CREATE AN ARCTIC TESTBED TO SUPPORT PROJECT DEVELOPMENT AND FACILITATE UPTAKE AND TRANSITION TO PRACTICE BY CONDUCTING RIGOROUS, TRANSPARENT, AND REPLICABLE TESTING OF SCIENTIFIC THEORIES, COMPUTING TOOLS, AND NEW TECHNOLOGIES WHILE EMBRACING HARSH ARCTIC CONDITIONS AND CHALLENGES. THE DIVERSITY, COORDINATION, AND COLLABORATION OF ADACARCTIC AND ITS COLLABORATORS, AND ITS CLOSE PARTNERSHIPS WITH DHS AND THE HSE AT-LARGE, WILL YIELD FRESH IDEAS, EXEMPLARY PROJECT APPLICABILITY, AND EFFECTIVE TRANSITIONS, ALL TO THE BENEFIT OF THE HSE IN THE ARCTIC.

CORRECTIONS AGENCIES ARE GRAPPLING WITH HOW TO CREATE SAFE AND HUMANE ENVIRONMENTS FOR PEOPLE WHO WORK, VISIT, AND ARE INCARCERATED IN PRISON; TO RECRUIT AND RETAIN STAFF; AND TO SUSTAIN EFFORTS THAT PROMOTE INCARCERATED PEOPLES SUCCESSFUL REENTRY TO THE COMMUNITY. TRANSFORMING THE CULTURES, CLIMATES, AND SPACES IN PRISONS IS ESSENTIAL TO ENHANCE SAFETY, IMPROVE THE DYNAMICS BETWEEN STAFF AND INCARCERATED PEOPLE, CREATE COMMUNITY AND A SENSE OF PURPOSE BEYOND CUSTODY AND CONTROL, AND SHAPE A CULTURE THAT CENTERS THE DIGNITY OF BOTH STAFF AND INCARCERATED PEOPLE. TO ADDRESS THE CRITICAL PROBLEM OF TRANSFORMING PRISON CULTURES, CLIMATES, AND SPACES, THE VERA INSTITUTE OF JUSTICE (VERA) IS EXPANDING ITS GROUNDBREAKING WORK OF RESTORING PROMISE THROUGH A NEW PROJECT, DESIGNED FOR DIGNITY.

VERA WILL INSPIRE AND BROADLY SUPPORT THE CORRECTIONS FIELD TO TRANSFORM ITS CULTURES, CLIMATES, AND SPACES BY SELECTING EIGHT DIVERSE AGENCIES TO USE THE DESIGNED FOR DIGNITY FRAMEWORKTO ASSESS AND TRANSFORM THEIR POLICIES, TRAINING, AND RESOURCE ALLOCATIONS SO THEY ARE BETTER ALIGNED WITH DIGNITY AND TO ACHIEVE THEIR MISSION-CRITICAL GOALS.

THE TRANSFORMATION PROCESS WILL BE SUCCESSFUL BY LEVERAGING THE LEADERSHIP OF TRAINED CORRECTIONS PROFESSIONALS AND INCARCERATED PEOPLE AND PROCEEDING IN THREE STAGES: LEARNING AND STRATEGY DESIGN, CHANGE MANAGEMENT, AND SUSTAINABILITY. BEYOND THE EIGHT AGENCIES SELECTED TO GET SUPPORT WITH THE DESIGNED FOR DIGNITY FRAMEWORK, VERA WILL PROVIDE SUPPORT TO THE FIELD BY DEVELOPING AND DISSEMINATING RESOURCES AND RESPONDING TO AD HOC REQUESTS. VERA WILL PROACTIVELY BUILD FIELD KNOWLEDGE AND CAPACITY THROUGHOUT THE COURSE OF THE PROJECTMAINTAINING AN UP-TO-DATE REVIEW OF THE LITERATURE, BEST PRACTICES IN CORRECTIONS, AND INNOVATIONS IN CORRECTIONS CULTURES, CLIMATES, AND SPACES.

BY COMBINING THE EXPERTISE OF CORRECTIONS PROFESSIONALS AND INCARCERATED PEOPLE WITH VERA'S EXPERIENCE IN ON THE GROUND, EVIDENCE-BASED PRISON TRANSFORMATION WORK, DESIGNED FOR DIGNITY WILL BRING ABOUT MEANINGFUL AND SUSTAINABLE CHANGES IN THE PARTICIPATING CORRECTIONAL AGENCIES AND BUILD FIELD KNOWLEDGE AND CAPACITY FOR TRANSFORMING PRISON CULTURES, CLIMATES, AND SPACES.DESIGNED FOR DIGNITY WILL RESULT IN GREATER SAFETY FOR ALL, SUCCESSFUL RE-ENTRY FOR INCARCERATED PEOPLE, AND STAFF WHO ARE WELL AND HAVE PURPOSE.

THE VERA INSTITUTE OF JUSTICE (VERA) WILL UTILIZE THIS FUNDING TO IMPLEMENT MUNICIPAL SAFETY HUBS, A NEW MODEL OF COMMUNITY-CENTERED SAFETY INFRASTRUCTURE IN LOCAL GOVERNMENT. VERA WILL PROVIDE TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE AND SUBAWARDS TO THE ALBUQUERQUE (NEW MEXICO) COMMUNITY SAFETY DEPARTMENT AND THE CITY OF RICHMOND (CALIFORNIA) COMMUNITY SERVICES DEPARTMENT, OFFICE OF NEIGHBORHOOD SAFETY TO CREATE AND SUSTAIN CIVILIAN-LED SAFETY HUBS. THESE SAFETY HUBS WILL UTILIZE A DATA-INFORMED, COMMUNITY-CENTERED, NEEDS-BASED PUBLIC HEALTH APPROACH TO ADDRESS PUBLIC SAFETY AND SOCIAL NEEDS, WITHOUT RELYING SOLELY ON TRADITIONAL LAW ENFORCEMENT RESPONSES. THE PROJECT FOCUSES ON REFINING A CIVILIAN-LED PUBLIC SAFETY PLAN, EXPANDING CAPACITY FOR COLLECTING AND ANALYZING PUBLIC SAFETY DATA, AND FOSTERING ENGAGEMENT AND ACCOUNTABILITY TO SYSTEM IMPACTED COMMUNITY STAKEHOLDERS. THIS PROJECT WILL FOCUS ON HIGH-NEED AREAS, ADDRESSING INCIDENTS RELATED TO MENTAL AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH ISSUES, DISTURBANCES, AND SURVIVAL BEHAVIORS THAT TOO OFTEN BECOME CRIMINALIZED WHEN THE ONLY AVAILABLE RESPONSE IS LAW ENFORCEMENT (E.G. BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CRISES, PUBLIC DISTURBANCES, LOITERING, UNWANTED PERSONS, PUBLIC INTOXICATION, AND TRESPASSING). ALSO, VERA WILL ENGAGE A DIVERSE CROSS-SECTION OF SYSTEM-IMPACTED RESIDENTS, CIVILIAN GOVERNMENT AGENCIES, COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS, AND LOCAL STAKEHOLDERS TO DEVELOP STRATEGIES, MECHANISMS, AND MEASURES OF SUCCESS FOR GREATER COORDINATION, INTEGRATION, AND ACCOUNTABILITY TO SYSTEM-IMPACTED COMMUNITIES IN ADVANCING A SHARED VISION OF PUBLIC SAFETY.

THE VERA INSTITUTE OF JUSTICES (VERA) RESHAPING PROSECUTION INITIATIVE SEEKS FUNDING TO ADDRESS INEQUITIES IN ACCESS TO DIVERSION PROGRAMS FOR JUSTICE-INVOLVED COMMUNITIES. VERA WILL PARTNER WITH PROSECUTORS AND COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS THAT SERVE JUSTICE-INVOLVED COMMUNITIES TO BUILD OR EXPAND A DIVERSION PROGRAM THAT ADDRESSES A HEALTH AND SAFETY NEED IN THE LOCAL COMMUNITY AND INCLUDES THE FOLLOWING FEATURES: (1) HAS NO AUTOMATIC EXCLUSIONS BASED ON CRIMINAL HISTORY, (2) HAS NO MANDATORY FINES OR FEES, (3) ADOPTS A NEEDS-BASED PUBLIC HEALTH APPROACH (AS OPPOSED TO AN OFFENSE-BASED APPROACH), (4) PROVIDES PROGRAMMING AND CASE MANAGEMENT THROUGH A COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATION, AND (5) CONSULTS JUSTICE-INVOLVED COMMUNITIES TO CREATE METRICS TO EVALUATE THE DIVERSION PROGRAM. EACH PARTNERSHIP WILL INCLUDE THREE MAIN COMPONENTS: COLLABORATION WITH A COMMUNITY PARTNER TO IMPLEMENT AND SUPPORT THEIR DIVERSION PROGRAM THROUGH RESEARCH SUPPORT AND OTHER RESOURCES, COLLABORATION WITH THE PROSECUTOR'S OFFICE TO IMPLEMENT RACIALLY EQUITABLE PROCESSES FOR DIVERSION REFERRALS, AND QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE RESEARCH TO COLLECT DATA FOR PROCESS AND OUTCOME EVALUATIONS OF DIVERSION PROGRAMS. VERA WILL ALSO PROVIDE SUBGRANTS TO THE COMMUNITY PARTNERS TO SUPPORT INCREASING DIVERSION CAPACITY.

EXPECTED PRODUCTS INCLUDE IMPLEMENTATION AND EVALUATION TOOLS SUCH AS GUIDES AND FACT SHEETS FOR BUILDING AND EVALUATING THE SUCCESS OF THE PREVIOUSLY DESCRIBED DIVERSION PROGRAMS; A REPORT TO SHARE LESSONS LEARNED AND QUALITATIVE AND QUANTITATIVE RESEARCH COLLECTED FROM THE PARTNERSHIPS, INCLUDING AROUND RECIDIVISM AND METRICS CHOSEN BY THE LOCAL COMMUNITY; AND A VERA-LED LEARNING COMMUNITY OF PAST PARTNERS TO SUPPORT SUSTAINABILITY AND HELP SPREAD SIMILAR DIVERSION PROGRAMS ACROSS THE FIELD.

DESCRIPTION:THIS AGREEMENT PROVIDES FUNDING UNDER THE INFLATION REDUCTION ACT (IRA). THE AGREEMENT PROVIDES FUNDING TO THE PENOBSCOT INDIAN NATION. SPECIFICALLY, THE PROJECT WILL WORK WITH A CONTRACTOR TO INSTALL UP TO 180 ENERGY EFFICIENT HEATING SYSTEMS IN TRIBAL HOUSING UNITS. THE COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT IS A PARTNERSHIP AMONG THE WABANAKI ALLIANCE. THE RECIPIENT WILL WORK WITH OTHER WABANAKI NATIONS AS SUBRECIPIENTS TO MANAGE THEIR OWN BUDGETS. EACH NATION WILL WORK WITH THE COMMUNITY TO IDENTIFY CANDIDATE HOMES FOR HEAT PUMP INSTALLATION. EACH NATION WILL WORK WITH THEIR OWN CONTRACTOR TO COMPLETE THE INSTALLATIONS. THE PROJECT WILL ALSO INCLUDE TRAINING FOR TRIBAL MEMBERSHIP TO MAINTAIN AND PROPERLY OPERATE THEIR HEAT PUMP UNITS TO PROMOTE EFFICIENCY AND EFFECTIVENESS. THE PROJECT WILL ALSO CREATE TRAINING AND LEARNING OPPORTUNITIES FOR AT LEAST TEN CITIZENS TO BECOME CERTIFIED RENEWABLE ENERGY TECHNICIANS. THE PROJECT WILL INCLUDE COMMUNITY OUTREACH AND EDUCATION RELATED TO CLIMATE RESILIENCE AND IMPROVING SUSTAINABILITY FOR MEMBERS OF WABANAKI NATIONS.ACTIVITIES:THE ACTIVITIES WILL ESTABLISH A CO-MANAGED PLAN AMONG FOUR THE WABANAKI TRIBES AS A CONSORTIUM. THE PENOBSCOT INDIAN NATION WILL BE THE GRANTEE AND MANAGE THE GRANT. THE CONSORTIUM WILL ESTABLISH CRITERIA FOR RECEIVING A HEAT PUMP TO ENSURE UNITS WITH THE GREATEST NEED ARE ADDRESSED. THE CONTRACT IMPLEMENTATION WILL BE EQUALLY DIVIDED AS SUB-AWARDS, DUE TO THE GEOGRAPHICAL DISTANCE BETWEEN THE FOUR TRIBES OF THE WABANAKI ALLIANCE. THIS SPREADS THE MANAGEMENT AND FUNDING AMONGST FOUR TRIBES AND HELPS TO ENSURE THAT HEAT PUMPS WILL BE DEPLOYED TO THE HOUSEHOLDS WITH THE GREATEST NEED. EACH TRIBE'S PROGRAM MANAGER WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR REPORTING THE PROGRAM EVALUATION AND SUBMITTING DATA TO THE PENOBSCOT INDIAN NATION FOR COMPILATION AND COLLABORATION. A PROPERTY NEEDS ASSESSMENT AND SITE VISIT WILL BE INCORPORATED IN THE APPLICATION PROCESS. THIS PROVIDES AN OPPORTUNITY FOR THE PROGRAM MANAGER TO IDENTIFY ADDITIONAL NEEDS TO BE ADDRESSED WITHIN THE HOME. THIS NEEDS ASSESSMENT WILL ALSO HELP DETERMINE THE SIZE OF THE HEAT PUMP THAT IS NEEDED FOR THE HOME. THIS IS CRUCIAL TO MAINTAINING A BUDGET WHILE INSTALLING THE MOST HEAT PUMPS IN HOMES. EACH TRIBE WILL MANAGE AN OPEN BIDDING PROCESS THAT WILL ENGAGE QUALIFIED VENDORS TO INSTALL THE HEAT PUMPS IN THE SELECTED HOMES. THE PROCUREMENT PROCESS WILL INCLUDE NATIVE PREFERENCE TO INCREASE ACCESS TO CONTRACTS FOR TRIBAL CITIZENS. CONTRACTS WILL BE BUNDLED BY TRIBE AND WILL VARY DEPENDING ON THE TRIBE. THE WABANAKI ALLIANCE WILL BE WORKING WITH EFFICIENCY MAINE TO MAXIMIZE THE VARIOUS INCENTIVES, REBATES, AND TAX CREDITS AVAILABLE FOR HEAT PUMPS. THIS PROGRAM IS EXPECTED TO INSTALL AT LEAST 45 HEAT PUMPS PER TRIBE, DEPENDING ON INCENTIVES AND CONTRACTOR BIDS. THE WABANAKI CONSORTIUM WILL HOLD QUARTERLY MEETINGS TO COORDINATE FOR THIS PROGRAM, AND TO DEVELOP THE RENEWABLE ENERGY TECHNICIAN TRAINING, THE RESIDENT OR TENANT MAINTENANCE TRAINING, AND THE OUTREACH MATERIALS FOR HOMEOWNERS.SUBRECIPIENT:SUBAWARDS TOTALING $725,751.60 ARE TO BE DISTRIBUTED TO THREE TRIBES; THE HOULTON BAND OF MALISEET INDIANS, MI'KMAQ NATION, AND PASSAMAQUODDY PLEASANT POINT. DESCRIPTION:THE COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT PROVIDES FUNDING TO THE VERMONT AGENCY OF HUMAN SERVICES TO IMPROVE THE HEALTH AND WELL-BEING OF LOW-INCOME IMMIGRANTS, REFUGEES, AND ASYLUM SEEKERS/ASYLEE HOUSEHOLDS IN BURLINGTON AND WINOOSKI, VERMONT, BY CREATING A COMMUNITY AMBASSADOR-LED HEALTHY AND ENERGY-EFFICIENT HOMES PROGRAM. THE PROPOSED ACTIVITIES WILL EXPAND THE CHAMPLAIN VALLEY OFFICE OF ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITY'S COMMUNITY AMBASSADOR PROGRAM TO INCLUDE ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE WORK. THE HEALTHY AND ENERGY-EFFICIENT HOMES PROGRAM WILL PROVIDE HOME ASSESSMENTS, EDUCATION, REPAIRS, AND IMPROVEMENTS, TO SUPPORT CLIMATE CHANGE RESILIENCY AND HOME ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH IMPROVEMENT, PARTICULARLY FOR COMMUNITY MEMBERS WITH POORLY CONTROLLED ASTHMA OR OTHER CONDITIONS AFFECTED BY HOME ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS. THE PROJECT INCLUDES ENGAGING WITH RESIDENTS AND COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS TO LEARN MORE ABOUT ENVIRONMENTAL BURDENS THROUGH COMMUNITY FORUMS AND COMMUNITY-BASED PARTICIPATORY RESEARCH AND EVALUATION. THIS PROJECT WILL PROVIDE DIRECT SERVICES, TRAINING AND EDUCATION ENGAGING LOCAL RESIDENTS TO IDENTIFY AND PLAN FOR LONG-TERM ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE ACTION. THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO BUILD A COMMUNITY AMBASSADOR ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE MODEL FOR EXPANSION INTO A STATEWIDE COMMUNITY INCLUSION NETWORK DESIGNED TO INCREASE ENGAGEMENT AND INCREASE SERVICES FOR UNDERSERVED RESIDENTS.ACTIVITIES:THE ACTIVITIES INCLUDE EXPANDING CHAMPLAIN VALLEY OFFICE OF ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITY'S (CVOEO) COMMUNITY AMBASSADOR PROGRAM TO INCLUDE ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE PROGRAMMING AND CREATING THE HEALTHY AND ENERGY-EFFICIENT HOMES PROGRAM. THE COMMUNITY AMBASSADORS WILL RECEIVE TRAINING TO IMPROVE AWARENESS AND UNDERSTANDING OF ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE CHALLENGES AND OPPORTUNITIES. FOLLOWING THE TRAINING, CVOEO COMMUNITY AMBASSADORS WILL CONDUCT SMALL-GROUP OUTREACH THROUGH IN-HOME GATHERINGS; FACILITATE NINE LANGUAGE SPECIFIC GATHERINGS, WHICH EACH WILL HAVE FOUR SESSIONS WITH PEOPLE FROM THE SAME CULTURE COMMUNITY COMING TOGETHER. ALONG WITH CVOEO AND THE UNIVERSITY OF VERMONT, THE RECIPIENT WILL DEVELOP A COMMUNITY-BASED PARTICIPATORY RESEARCH AND EVALUATION APPROACH AND ENGAGE IN THE BROADER COMMUNITY THROUGH SURVEYS AND ANNUAL COMMUNITY FORUMS. THE RECIPIENT WILL COLLECT COMMUNITY INPUT ON HEALTHY HOUSING AND ENERGY EFFICIENCY NEEDS TO INFORM THE LAUNCH OF THE HEALTHY AND ENERGY-EFFICIENT HOMES PROGRAM. THIS PROGRAM WILL OFFER HEALTHY HOUSING AND ENERGY EFFICIENCY ASSESSMENTS TO 100 HOMES AND SUPPORT REPAIRS, IMPROVEMENTS, AND SUPPLIES TO 50 OF THOSE HOMES. HOME ASSESSMENTS WILL INCLUDE A PROFESSIONAL WALK THROUGH AND INTERVIEW WITH THE OCCUPANTS TO IDENTIFY POTENTIAL ENVIRONMENTAL HAZARDS AND ENERGY EFFICIENCY OPPORTUNITIES. grants.description: THE AGREEMENT PROVIDES FUNDING TO RHODE ISLAND DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT (RIDEM) TO STRENGTHEN COMMUNITY CONNECTIONS AND BUILD A COLLECTIVE UNDERSTANDING OF ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE CONCERNS IN THE UPPER NARRAGANSETT BAY WATERSHED, WHICH IS CONNECTED BY THE PROVIDENCE, BLACKSTONE, WOONASQUATUCKET, AND MOSHASSUCK RIVERS. THE PROJECT PARTNERS IN COLLABORATION WITH RIDEM WILL TRAIN A COHORT OF PROGRAM STAFF FROM ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL SERVICE COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS IN PROVIDENCE, CENTRAL FALLS, PAWTUCKET, AND WOONSOCKET THROUGH A SERIES OF ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE (EJ) WORKSHOPS AND ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH PRESENTATIONS. THE GOAL IS TO BUILD A SHARED UNDERSTANDING OF ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE ISSUES, HISTORY, AND PRACTICES AND STRENGTHEN COMMUNITY AND GOVERNMENT CONNECTIONS ACROSS THE WATERSHED. TECHNICAL PRESENTATIONS ON TOPICS INCLUDING AIR QUALITY, WATER QUALITY, TREE EQUITY, AND CLIMATE CHANGE IMPACTS WILL BE PROVIDED TO THIS COHORT BY RIDEM AND PROJECT PARTNERS. MEMBERS OF THIS COHORT WILL RECEIVE TRAINING AND MATERIALS ON RESIDENTIAL PROGRAMS RELATED TO ENERGY SAVINGS AND FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE TO EMPOWER RESIDENTS IN THEIR COMMUNITIES TO MITIGATE THE IMPACTS OF ENVIRONMENTAL HAZARDS IN HOMES. BEYOND THIS TRAINING CURRICULUM, SUBRECIPIENTS WILL ENGAGE IN COMMUNITY EVENTS AND PROGRAM ACTIVITIES TO ENGAGE RESIDENTS FROM THE LOCAL COMMUNITIES. THE INTENDED OUTCOMES INCLUDE INCREASED COMMUNITY UNDERSTANDING OF ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE ISSUES, ENGAGEMENT IN POLICY DECISION-MAKING, AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF A SUSTAINABLE MODEL FOR FUTURE COLLABORATION IN THE UPPER NARRAGANSETT BAY WATERSHED, WHICH CONNECTS THE ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE AREAS OF PROVIDENCE, CENTRAL FALLS, AND PAWTUCKET.FIVE SUBAWARDS WILL BE ALLOCATED TO FIVE DIFFERENT ENTITIES. SUBAWARD 1 WILL PROVIDE FUNDING TO THE WOONASQUATUCKET RIVER WATERSHED COUNCIL TO PROVIDE ASSISTANCE WITH FACILITATION, TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE, AND  PROGRAM ADMINISTRATION. THE WOONASQUATUCKET RIVER WATERSHED COUNCIL WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR ADMINISTERING COMMUNITY PARTICIPANT STIPENDS, THE DEVELOPMENT AND HOSTING OF THE WEB RESOURCE PORTAL, AND PROVIDING EQUIPMENT TO SUPPORT COMMUNITY TOURS. SUBAWARD 2 WILL PROVIDE FUNDING FOR THE RACIAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE COMMITTEE TO CONDUCT SIX COMMUNITY WORKSHOPS ON THE IMPACTS OF ENVIRONMENTAL HAZARDS AND ENVIRONMENTAL RACISM AND COMMIT UP TO 200 HOURS TOWARD COHORT PLANNING. THE RACIAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE COMMITTEE WILL ALSO USE FUNDS FOR PRINT MATERIALS, SUPPLIES AND PARTICIPANT GIFT CARDS RELATED TO THEIR WORKSHOPS. SUBAWARD 3 WILL PROVIDE FUNDING TO MOVEMENT EDUCATION OUTDOORS TO PROVIDE ONE EDUCATIONAL WORKSHOP SERIES AND UP TO 200 HOURS OF COHORT PLANNING, CURRICULUM DEVELOPMENT AND SUPPORT FOR THE PROJECT. SUBAWARD 4 WILL PROVIDE FUNDING TO IMPACT RI TO PROVIDE UP TO 2,000 HOURS OF STAFF SUPPORT TO ASSIST IN THE DISTRIBUTION OF INFORMATION INTO UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES WHO WILL BE DIRECTLY EFFECTED BY NATURAL DISASTER AND ENVIRONMENTAL HAZARDS IN RHODE ISLAND'S AIR AND RIVERS. SUBAWARD 5 WILL PROVIDE FUNDING TO THE NATURE CONSERVANCY FOR A PROGRAM MANAGER TO OVERSEE THE PROJECT. THE PROGRAM MANAGER WILL BE PARTICIPATE IN THE PROGRAM STEERING COMMITTEE, HELP DEVELOP CURRICULUM FOR WORKSHOPS AND PARTICIPATE IN THE WORKSHOPS. THE ACTIVITIES COVERED BY THIS PROJECT INCLUDE HOSTING WORKSHOPS AND TRAINING ACTIVITIES, CREATION OF VIDEOS, ARTWORK, AND OTHER OUTREACH MATERIALS, DEVELOPMENT OF A COMMUNITY RESOURCES WEB PORTAL, AND CONVENING COMMUNITY STAKEHOLDERS TO BUILD COMMUNITY CAPACITY FOR PARTICIPATION IN DECISION-MAKING AT THE STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT LEVEL. MEMBERS OF THE TRAINING COHORT WILL RECEIVE TRAINING AND MATERIALS ON RESIDENTIAL PROGRAMS RELATED TO ENERGY SAVINGS AND FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE TO EMPOWER RESIDENTS IN THEIR COMMUNITIES TO MITIGATE THE IMPACTS OF ENVIRONMENTAL HAZARDS IN HOMES. BEYOND THIS TRAINING CURRICULUM, SUBRECIPIENTS WILL ENGAGE IN COMMUNITY EVENTS AND PROGRAM ACTIVITIES TO ENGAGE RESIDENTS FROM THE LOCAL COMMUNITIES TO SUPPORT EMPOWERMENT IN LOCAL DECISION MAKING ON ENVIRONMENT AND PUBLIC HEALTH ISSUES IN COMMUNITIES NEAR THE PROVIDENCE, BLACKSTONE, WOONASQUATUCKET AND MOSHASSUCK RIVERS.THE ACTIVITIES OF THIS GRANT INCLUDE DEVELOPING AN ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE TRAINING SERIES OF PROGRAM STAFF FROM COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS. DESCRIPTION:THE PURPOSE OF THIS ARP FUNDED GRANT AGREEMENT IS TO USE AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN (ARP) APPROPRIATIONS TO PARTNER WITH THE YALE UNIVERSITY URBAN DESIGN WORKGROUP TO CONDUCT A COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT AND PLANNING PROCESS TO ADDRESS AIR QUALITY AND URBAN HEAT ISLAND ISSUES IMPACTING LOCAL RESIDENTS. THE PROJECT, CONDUCTED BY THE GREATER DWIGHT DEVELOPMENT CORPORATION, BASED IN NEW HAVEN, CT, WILL DEVELOP RESEARCH ON LOCAL ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS IN THE NEIGHBORHOOD, INCLUDING AIR QUALITY MONITORING; AND DEVELOP A WEB-BASED NEIGHBORHOOD PLANNING DOCUMENT, INCLUDING A GEOGRAPHIC INFORMATION SYSTEM (GIS), REAL-TIME DASHBOARD OF AIR QUALITY IN THE NEIGHBORHOOD FOR USE BY LOCAL RESIDENTS. THIS PROJECT WILL IMPROVE RESIDENT UNDERSTANDING OF ENVIRONMENT AND PUBLIC HEALTH ISSUES, IMPROVE AIR QUALITY AND GREEN SPACE FROM ADDED TREES, PLANTS, AND SHADE; AND EXPAND SOCIALIZATION OPPORTUNITIES THROUGH ACTIVITIES WITH OTHER RESIDENTS, FAMILIES, AND NEIGHBORS. THIS PROJECT SUPPORTS THE CLEAN AIR ACT (CAA) 103(B)(3): PEOPLE WITH MODERATE-TO-SEVERE OR UNCONTROLLED ASTHMA ARE MORE LIKELY TO BE HOSPITALIZED FROM COVID-19. AIR POLLUTION MAY CONTRIBUTE TO ASTHMA. BY ADDRESSING AIR POLLUTION IN CAA 103(B)(3) PROJECTS, THE CHANCES OF SEVERE ILLNESS FROM COVID-19 ARE REDUCED.
ACTIVITIES:THE PROJECT HAS THREE COMPONENTS: TO RESEARCH AND DOCUMENT URBAN AND ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS IN THE NEIGHBORHOOD WHICH IMPACT RESIDENT HEALTH, CONTRIBUTING TO A COMPREHENSIVE UNDERSTANDING OF UNDERLYING ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS, INCLUDING EXPANDING A NEIGHBORHOOD SCALE AIR QUALITY MONITORING NETWORK TO PROVIDE A NEW, COMMUNITY-OWNED DATASET THAT WILL BE USED FOR ONGOING AND FUTURE PLANNING EFFORTS; TO ENGAGE AND INFORM NEIGHBORHOOD RESIDENTS IN A PLANNING PROCESS THAT CREATES LEARNING FOR PLANNERS AND COMMUNITY MEMBERS THROUGH A SERIES OF OPEN CHARRETTE-STYLE ACTIVITIES, OPEN HOUSES, WALKING TOURS, A SCAVENGER HUNT, AND MEETINGS FOCUSED ON HEALTH AND THE URBAN ENVIRONMENT, INCLUDING A YOUTH EDUCATION COMPONENT TO DEVELOP AN ACTIONABLE NEIGHBORHOOD PLAN WITH PRIORITIES THAT GUIDES FUTURE ACTIVITIES TO IMPROVE HEALTH AND THE ENVIRONMENT. DESCRIPTION:THIS ACTION APPROVES AN AWARD IN THE AMOUNT OF $1,000,000 TO SUPPORT THE MOBILE COUNTY BOARD OF HEALTH (MCHD) TO EXPAND THE LEAD POISONING PREVENTION (LPP) PROGRAM ACTIVITIES WITH THE GOAL OF REDUCING THE NUMBER OF CHILDREN EXPOSED TO LEAD IN MOBILE COUNTY. MCHD WILL FOCUS ON THE FOLLOWING OBJECTIVES: INCREASE SOIL TESTING IN MOBILE COUNTY, INCREASE COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT AND ADVOCACY AROUND LPP, INCREASE AWARENESS OF THE HAZARDS OF LEAD EXPOSURE AND KNOWLEDGE OF HOW TO RESPOND, INCREASE CAPACITY FOR LOW-INCOME COMMUNITIES TO COMPLETE REMEDIATION PROJECT AND ESTABLISH A REFERRAL NETWORK AND ROADMAP TO SUPPORT FAMILIES EXPOSED TO LEAD. THE ANTICIPATED ACTIVITIES INCLUDE CONDUCTING QUARTERLY SOIL TESTING CLINICS, COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT MEETINGS, CASE MANAGEMENT FOR FAMILIES WITH HIGH SOIL LEAD LEVELS (SLLS), MARKETING, AND EDUCATIONAL OUTREACH. WE HAVE SELECTED FOUR COMMUNITIES WITHIN MOBILE COUNTY TO TARGET ACTIVITIES; THESE ARE COMMUNITIES THAT WE KNOW, BASED ON EXISTING DATA, ARE LOW-INCOME AND HIGH RISK FOR LEAD EXPOSURE DUE TO AGING HOUSING AND THE PROXIMITY TO HIGHWAYS AND INDUSTRY. THE ANTICIPATED DELIVERABLES INCLUDE CONDUCTING FOUR SOIL TESTING CLINICS ANNUALLY AND PROVIDE FEEDBACK TO STAKEHOLDERS IN THE TARGETED AREA; HOST COMMUNITY MEETINGS WITH FAMILIES TO INCREASE LEAD AWARENESS; DEVELOP AND EXECUTE A MARKETING CAMPAIGN RELATED TO LEAD PREVENTION; AND ESTABLISH A SMALL GRANT PROGRAM FOR LOW-INCOME FAMILIES WHERE LEAD WAS DETECTED.  THE EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE NUMBER OF SOIL SAMPLES COLLECTED AND TESTED; NUMBER OF PARTICIPATION RATE OF COMMUNITY MEETINGS HELD TO DISCUSS THE MAPS AND EDUCATION AROUND LEAD POISONING PREVENTION; NUMBER OF ONE-ON-ONE CONSULTATIONS WITH FAMILIES WHO RECEIVED HIGH SLL RESULTS; NUMBER OF GRANTS DISTRIBUTED TO LOW-INCOME RESIDENTS; AND NUMBER OF REFERRALS CLOSED SUCCESSFULLY. THE INTENDED BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE THESE AREAS: PRICHARD, AFRICATOWN, DAUPHIN ISLAND PARKWAY, CITY OF THEODORE, BAYOU LA BATRE, AND THE MOWA CHOCTAW TRIBE.ACTIVITIES:.SUBRECIPIENT:1. DESCRIPTION:THE AGREEMENT PROVIDES FUNDING TO MUNICIPALITY OF VEGA BAJA. SPECIFICALLY, THE RECIPIENT WILL ASSIST COMMUNITIES IN IDENTIFYING, PREVENTING, AND ELIMINATING BLIGHTED PROPERTIES AND ASSOCIATED HEALTH AND ENVIRONMENTAL RISKS. THE PROJECT WILL ENABLE COMMUNITIES TO IDENTIFY AND MAP ASSETS, CHALLENGES, AND OPPORTUNITIES, PARTICIPATE IN PLANNING ACTIVITIES TO CREATE A REUSE PLAN, AND CONCEPTUALIZE, ASSESS THE VIABILITY OF, AND EXECUTE PILOT MITIGATION PROJECTS FROM THE REUSE PLAN.ACTIVITIES:THE ACTIVITIES INCLUDE EDUCATION, TRAINING, CIVIC ENGAGEMENT, COMMUNITY MAPPING AND REUSE PLANNING, AND SMALL-SCALE ACQUISITION AND MITIGATION. INTERACTIVE TRAININGS ON COMMUNITY MAPPING AND THE IDENTIFICATION OF AND RISKS RELATED TO BLIGHT WILL BE DELIVERED. TRAINING PARTICIPANTS WILL WORK WITH PROJECT PARTNERS TO MAP POTENTIAL NUISANCE PROPERTIES AND THEIR ENVIRONMENTAL AND HEALTH RISKS. FOLLOW-UP MAPPING WILL BE CONDUCTED THROUGHOUT THE PROJECT PERIOD. COMMUNITY PLANNING WORKSHOPS WILL BE HELD TO REVIEW MAPPING RESULTS, CONSULT WITH THE COMMUNITY, DRAFT A REUSE PLAN, SEEK FEEDBACK, AND PUBLISH A FINAL REUSE PLAN. TRAININGS ON BEST PRACTICES FOR REDUCTION, PREVENTION, AND REUSE, AS WELL AS CAPACITY BUILDING FOR REUSE PLAN IMPLEMENTATION, WILL BE DELIVERED. PILOT PROJECTS SELECTED FROM THE REUSE PLAN WILL BE CARRIED OUT AND MAY INCLUDE DECONSTRUCTION, DEMOLITION, REHABILITATION, CLEAN-UP, OR ABATEMENT. THE APPROPRIATE ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW AND CONSTRUCTION CROSSCUTTERS WILL BE ADDRESSED PRIOR TO STARTING ANY CONSTRUCTION ACTIVITIES. SUBRECIPIENT:THE CENTER FOR HABITAT RECONSTRUCTION IS A SUBRECIPIENT. DAY-TO-DAY OPERATIONS OF THE PROJECT WILL BE EXECUTED BY CENTER FOR HABITAT RECONSTRUCTION, WHICH INCLUDES SUPPORTING THE MUNICIPALITY OF VEGA BAJA IN FACILITATING OUTREACH AND EDUCATION TRAININGS, COMMUNITY MAPPING AND PLANNING, AND CAPACITY BUILDING TRAININGS. CENTER FOR HABITAT RECONSTRUCTION WILL ALSO EXECUTE NATURE-BASED PILOT PROJECTS AND NUISANCE CLEAN UP AND ABATEMENT, AND COMPLETE REQUIRED ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW AND CONSTRUCTION CROSSCUTTER COMPLIANCE BEFORE ANY CONSTRUCTION ACTIVITIES TAKE PLACE.OUTCOMES:THE ANTICIPATED DELIVERABLES INCLUDE TRAINED RESIDENTS, PRE- AND POST-EVALUATIONS, COMMUNITY MAPS, ONE REUSE PLAN, MEETINGS WITH POLICYMAKERS AND ADVOCATES, AN ANTICIPATED FIVE DECONSTRUCTIONS OR DEMOLITIONS, SIXTEEN CLEAN-UP OR ABATEMENT INTERVENTIONS, SIX REHABILITATED AFFORDABLE HOUSING UNITS FOR CLIMATE RESILIENCY AND ADAPTATION, SIX SMALL-SCALE NATURE-BASED PROJECTS, AND SEMI-ANNUAL AND FINAL REPORTS. THE EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE AN INCREASE IN THE NUMBER OF HEALTH AND ENVIRONMENTAL RISKS IDENTIFIED AND MAPPED IN COMMUNITIES, INCREASED KNOWLEDGE AND AWARENESS OF BLIGHT AND ITS RISK, REDUCTION, AND PREVENTION AMONG RESIDENTS, INCREASED MAPPING KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS AMONG COMMUNITY MEMBERS, INCREASED RESIDENT COMMITMENT TO AND MEANINGFUL ENGAGEMENT IN BLIGHT REDUCTION AND PREVENTION, AND INCREASED CAPACITY AND RESILIENCE IN OVERBURDENED AND UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES. THE PROJECT IS EXPECTED TO INCREASE INTERVENTION FOR NUISANCE PROPERTIES THROUGH MITIGATION OF FINDINGS AND IMPLEMENTATION OF RECOMMENDATIONS IN THE REUSE PLAN, THEREBY DECREASING ENVIRONMENTAL AND HEALTH RISKS IN THE COMMUNITY. THE INTENDED BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE THE MUNICIPALITY OF VEGA BAJA, AS WELL AS ITS RESIDENTS AND PROJECT PARTNERS.

THIS AGREEMENT SUPPORTS THE RECIPIENT'S PROJECT TO ESTABLISH THE NEW JERSEY EJ EDUCATION COLLABORATIVE.  THE PROJECT AIMS TO PROVIDE TRAINING IN EJ AND ENHANCE THE CAPACITY OF EJ COMMUNITIES, EMPOWERING RESIDENTS TO ENGAGE IN PUBLIC DISCOURSE ON ISSUES AFFECTING THEM. THROUGH THE PROJECT, RESIDENTS WILL BE EDUCATED ON HOW TO ADVOCATE FOR THEIR COMMUNITY'S BEST INTERESTS IN DISCUSSIONS WITH GOVERNMENT AND PRIVATE ENTITIES REGARDING SITING, PERMITTING AND OTHER DECISIONS AFFECTING THEIR ENVIRONMENT. THESE COMMUNITIES ARE HISTORICALLY DIFFICULT TO REACH, ENGAGE AND ORGANIZE, WHICH IS WHY GRASSROOTS ORGANIZATIONS ARE CRITICAL TO THIS MISSION. THE NJ EJ LAW REQUIRES ENHANCED PUBLIC ENGAGEMENT FOR RESIDENTS IN EJ COMMUNITIES, ALLOWING THEM TO DEMONSTRATE LOCAL IMPACT AND HAVE PERMITS DENIED. THIS HAS ACCELERATED THE NEED TO TRAIN EJ COMMUNITIES SO THEY CAN EFFECTIVELY INFLUENCE THIS DEMOCRATIC PROCESS.

NJDEP WILL ALSO RETOOL EDUCATIONAL CONTENT AND PILOT THE CURRICULUM WITH A HUB LEADER SEMINAR. DESCRIPTION:THIS AGREEMENT PROVIDES FUNDING UNDER THE INFLATION REDUCTION ACT TO SOCIEDAD AMBIENTE MARINO TO IMPROVE THE ADAPTIVE CAPACITY OF UNDERSERVED COASTAL COMMUNITIES IN PUERTO RICO TO CLIMATE CHANGE IMPACTS THROUGH LOCALLY-LED ADAPTATION PLANNING. 

THE PROJECT WILL WORK WITH THREE COMMUNITIES SARDINAS IN CULEBRA, LA MARGARITA IN SALINAS, AND LA 23 IN LOIACUTE;ZA. SOCIEDAD AMBIENTE MARINO WILL COORDINATE REGIONAL CITIZEN CLIMATE DIALOGUES TO DEFINE LOCAL AND NATIONAL PRIORITIES FOR RESILIENCE PLANNING. THEY WILL CONDUCT WORKSHOPS AND TRAINING SESSIONS TO STRENGTHEN THE TECHNICAL CAPACITY OF LOCAL ACTORS AND GOVERNMENTS IN PARTICIPATORY DECISION-MAKING FOR CLIMATE ADAPTATION. THE PROJECT WILL ALSO DEVELOP COMMUNITY CLIMATE ADAPTATION PLANS WITH RESIDENTS AND INTEGRATE THESE INTO LOCAL AND NATIONAL PLANNING PROCESSES. 

THE PROJECT AIMS TO EMPOWER LOCAL COMMUNITIES TO LEAD THEIR OWN ADAPTATION EFFORTS, BUILDING LONG-TERM RESILIENCE AND IMPROVING CLIMATE GOVERNANCE IN PUERTO RICO. THIS WORK ADDRESSES CRITICAL ENVIRONMENTAL ISSUES FACING THESE COASTAL COMMUNITIES, INCLUDING SEA LEVEL RISE, FLOODING, HURRICANES, AND OTHER CLIMATE-RELATED RISKS. BY FOCUSING ON LOCALLY-LED ADAPTATION, COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT, AND PARTICIPATORY PLANNING, THE PROJECT SEEKS TO CREATE MORE EFFECTIVE AND EQUITABLE CLIMATE SOLUTIONS FOR PUERTO RICO'S MOST VULNERABLE POPULATIONS.ACTIVITIES:THE ACTIVITIES TO BE PERFORMED BY THE PUERTO RICO PLANNING FOR LOCALLY-LED ADAPTATION PROJECT INCLUDE HOSTING A MULTILEVEL LAUNCH EVENT TO INTRODUCE THE INITIATIVE TO VARIOUS STAKEHOLDERS, FACILITATING FIVE REGIONAL CITIZEN CLIMATE ASSEMBLIES TO GATHER INPUT AND BUILD CONSENSUS ON LOCAL AND NATIONAL CLIMATE PRIORITIES, AND DEVELOP AND CONDUCT TRAINING SESSIONS FOR BOTH POLICY MAKERS AND COMMUNITY MEMBERS. THESE SESSIONS WILL FOCUS ON CLIMATE CHANGE ADAPTATION PLANNING, LOCALLY-LED ADAPTATION APPROACHES, AND EFFECTIVE PUBLIC PARTICIPATION STRATEGIES. 

THE PROJECT AIMS TO ESTABLISH A COMMUNITY OF PRACTICE AROUND THESE TOPICS, CULMINATING IN AN ISLAND-WIDE KNOWLEDGE-SHARING EVENT. A KEY COMPONENT OF THE PROJECT INVOLVES WORKING DIRECTLY WITH THREE COASTAL COMMUNITIES: SARDINAS IN CULEBRA, LA MARGARITA IN SALINAS, AND LA 23 IN LOIACUTE;ZA. IN EACH COMMUNITY, THE TEAM WILL HOST PARTICIPATORY MEETINGS TO IDENTIFY AND PRIORITIZE CLIMATE RISKS AND POTENTIAL SOLUTIONS. THIS INPUT WILL BE USED TO DEVELOP COMPREHENSIVE COMMUNITY CLIMATE ADAPTATION PLANS. ONCE DEVELOPED, THESE PLANS WILL BE PRESENTED TO LOCAL GOVERNMENTS FOR INTEGRATION INTO MUNICIPAL AND REGIONAL PLANNING PROCESSES. THE PROJECT WILL ALSO SUPPORT THE IMPLEMENTATION OF AT LEAST THREE COMMUNITY-DESIGNED PILOT INTERVENTIONS TO ADDRESS SPECIFIC CLIMATE ADAPTATION NEEDS. 

THROUGHOUT THE PROJECT PERIOD, THE TEAM WILL CONDUCT QUARTERLY MEETINGS WITH STAKEHOLDERS TO DEVELOP IMPLEMENTATION ROADMAPS AND ENSURE THE SUSTAINABILITY OF THESE LOCALLY-LED ADAPTATION EFFORTS. ONGOING EVALUATION AND REPORTING WILL BE CARRIED OUT TO TRACK PROGRESS AND ADJUST STRATEGIES AS NEEDED. THROUGH THESE ACTIVITIES, THE PROJECT AIMS TO EMPOWER LOCAL COMMUNITIES TO LEAD THEIR OWN CLIMATE ADAPTATION EFFORTS AND IMPROVE OVERALL CLIMATE GOVERNANCE IN PUERTO RICO.SUBRECIPIENT:THE ACTIVITIES TO BE IMPLEMENTED THROUGH SUBAWARDS FOCUS ON GOAL 3 OF THE PLALLA WORK PLAN: INCORPORATING LOCALLY-LED ADAPTATION CONSIDERATIONS INTO COMMUNITY, LOCAL, AND NATIONAL PLANNING PROCESSES. THE THREE COMMUNITIES - COMUNIDAD SARDINAS IN CULEBRA, COMUNIDAD LA MARGARITA IN SALINAS, AND COMUNIDAD LA 23 IN LOIACUTE;ZA - WILL PLAY CRUCIAL ROLES IN THIS PROCESS.

SUBAWARD RECIPIENTS ASOCIACIOACUTE;N DE RESIDENTES DE LA MARGARITA AND TALLER SALUD, ALONG WITH A COMMUNITY ORGANIZATION IN CULEBRA, WILL LEAD EFFORTS IN THEIR RESPECTIVE COMMUNITIES TO HOST PARTICIPATORY MEETINGS. THESE MEETINGS WILL IDENTIFY, DISCUSS, AND PRIORITIZE CLIMATE RISKS AND SOLUTIONS WITH COMMUNITY RESIDENTS, TAKING INTO CONSIDERATION THEIR SOCIO-ECONOMIC CONTEXT. THE SUBAWARD RECIPIEN

THE RECIPIENT WILL TRAIN UNDESERVED, DIVERSE STUDENTS AND RESIDENTS OF THE BRONX AS WELL AS YONKERS AND MOUNT VERNON IN WESTCHESTER COUNTY, NEW YORK ABOUT WATER QUALITY ISSUES AFFECTING THEIR COMMUNITY. THROUGH WATER QUALITY SAMPLING, STUDENTS AND RESIDENTS WILL LEARN ABOUT THE HEALTH OF THEIR LOCAL ECOSYSTEM AND ITS WATER QUALITY. THE PROJECT WILL ENABLE HIRING AN URBAN WATERWAYS ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE FELLOW RECRUITED FROM LOCAL COMMUNITIES WHO WILL WORK WITH LOCAL STAKEHOLDERS TO CARRY OUT PATHOGEN WATER QUALITY MONITORING, ADDITIONAL MONITORING OF HIGH POLLUTING OUTFALLS IDENTIFIED THROUGH THE PROJECT, AND EDNA TESTING. DATA REVEALING THE ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH OF THESE WATERWAYS FOR PEOPLE AND WILDLIFE WILL BE ANALYZED AND VISUALIZED TO BE ACCESSIBLE AND USEFUL TO THE PUBLIC. PUBLIC EDUCATION AND OUTREACH INCLUDING COMMUNITY-BASED MACROINVERTEBRATE STUDIES AND PUBLIC EVENTS WILL TAKE PLACE WITH STAKEHOLDERS IN EACH COMMUNITY TO DISCUSS SOLUTIONS TO REGIONAL WATER QUALITY ISSUES.ACTIVITIES:THE ACTIVITIES INCLUDE PATHOGEN WATER QUALITY MONITORING, ADDITIONAL MONITORING OF HIGH POLLUTING OUTFALLS IDENTIFIED THROUGH THE PROJECT, AND EDNA TESTING. AS WELL AS, PUBLIC EDUCATION AND OUTREACH INCLUDING COMMUNITY-BASED MACROINVERTEBRATE STUDIES AND PUBLIC EVENTS WILL TAKE PLACE WITH STAKEHOLDERS IN EACH COMMUNITY TO DISCUSS SOLUTIONS TO REGIONAL WATER QUALITY ISSUES. THE RECIPIENT WILL USE EDUCATION AND TRAINING TO INCREASE AWARENESS OF HOW CRITICAL ENVIRONMENTAL ISSUES IMPACT THE HEALTH OF RESIDENTS AND THE LOCAL ECOSYSTEM.SUBRECIPIENT:BRONX RIVER ALLIANCE, INC WILL ISSUE SUBAWARDS UNDER THIS COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT. OUTCOMES:THE ANTICIPATED DELIVERABLES INCLUDE PROJECT QAPP APPROVED BY EPA, PATHOGEN SAMPLES COLLECTED AND ANALYZED, DNA SAMPLES COLLECTED AND ANALYZED, COMMUNITY SCIENCE VOLUNTEERS TRAINED, ENGLISH LANGUAGE ONE-PAGERS PRODUCED, 25 TRANSLATED-PAGERS (5 LANGUAGES TOTAL),  OUTREACH EVENTS, PUBLIC MEETINGS, SOCIAL MEDIA POSTS AND A MAINSTREAM MEDIA ARTICLE.
EXPECTED OUTCOMES AND OUTPUTS ARE TO INCREASE COMMUNITY AWARENESS OF THE WATER ISSUES AND THEIR POTENTIAL HEALTH EFFECTS, EDUCATIONAL CONTENT FOR STUDENTS AND COMMUNITY MEMBERS FOR BOTH IN-PERSON AND ONLINE. THE INTENDED BENEFICIARIES FOR THIS PROJECT ARE STUDENTS AND RESIDENTS OF UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES IN THE BRONX AND WESTCHESTER COUNTIES, NEW YORK.

DESCRIPTION:THE PURPOSE OF THIS ARP FUNDED GRANT IS TO TRAIN YOUTH LEADERS IN THE SOUTH BRONX SECTION OF THE BRONX, NEW YORK ON THE POTENTIAL ENVIRONMENTAL AND HEALTH EFFECTS OF AIR QUALITY AND HOW TO MITIGATE AIR POLLUTION IN THEIR COMMUNITY.   IN ADDITION, YOUTH MINISTRIES FOR PEACE AND JUSTICE, YMPJ, WILL CONDUCT AN ANALYSIS OF AIR QUALITY DATA COLLECTED IN THE SOUTH BRONX TO DETERMINE CORRELATION BETWEEN SOUTH BRONX AIR QUALITY, AIR POLLUTION, RESPIRATORY ILLNESS AND THE LINK BETWEEN AIR QUALITY AND COVID-TRANSMISSION AND POOR HEALTH. THE RESULT OF THE ANALYSIS WILL BE WIDELY DISSEMINATED, IN THE FORM OF TRAININGS, SPEAKER SERIES; PUBLIC OUTREACH AND EDUCATION ACTIVITIES, AND A VIRTUAL SYMPOSIUM, TO INCREASE AWARENESS AND TO PROVIDE RESIDENTS WITH CONTINUED EDUCATION ON THE CAUSES AND DELETERIOUS EFFECTS OF AIR POLLUTION INCLUDING COVID-19 AND THE STEPS COMMUNITY MEMBERS CAN TAKE TO PROTECT THEMSELVES FROM AIR POLLUTION EXPOSURE AND POOR HEALTH OUTCOMES. DIRECT BENEFICIARIES ARE RESIDENTS OF THE SOUTH BRONX SECTION OF THE BRONX, NEW YORK.
ACTIVITIES:YMPJ HAS COLLECTED HYPER-LOCAL AIR QUALITY DATA IN THE SOUTH BRONX SINCE 2009. THEY WILL NOW ANALYZE THIS DATA TO UNDERSTAND THE SPECIFIC CONNECTION BETWEEN SOUTH BRONX AIR QUALITY, INCIDENCE OF RESPIRATORY CONDITIONS, AND LINKS TO COVID-19 TRANSMISSION/OUTCOMES. YMPJ WILL INFORM SOUTH BRONX RESIDENTS OF THE AIR POLLUTION AND EFFECTS ON RESPIRATORY HEALTH, WHAT CAN BE DONE TO INCREASE AIR QUALITY, AND STEPS COMMUNITY MEMBERS CAN TAKE TO PROTECT THEMSELVES FROM AIR POLLUTANTS INCLUDING COVID-19. YMPJ WILL TRAIN 60 YOUTH LEADERS, AGES 14-24, ON THE DELETERIOUS EFFECTS OF AIR POLLUTION ON RESPIRATORY HEALTH CONDITIONS INCLUDING COVID-19. A SIGNIFICANT FOCUS OF THE TRAINING SESSIONS WILL BE THE RELATED ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE ISSUES FACED BY SOUTH BRONX COMMUNITIES AND WHAT COMMUNITIES, NYC, NYS, AND THE FEDERAL GOVERNMENT CAN DO TO MITIGATE AIR POLLUTION. YMPJ WILL CONDUCT OUTREACH AND EDUCATION TO INFORM SOUTH BRONX RESIDENTS AND ALLAY FEARS ABOUT COVID 19 VACCINES AND BOOSTER SHOTS, AND INCREASE AWARENESS OF THE DETRIMENTAL EFFECTS OF AIR POLLUTION. YMPJ COMMUNITY OUTREACH SPECIALISTS WILL BE EQUIPPED TO HELP MAKE APPOINTMENTS ON THE SPOT USING INTERNET-ACCESSIBLE TABLETS. TO CULMINATE THE PROJECT, YMPJ WILL HOST A VIRTUAL SYMPOSIUM TO SHARE AIR QUALITY DATA AND COMMUNITY HEALTH ANALYSIS.SUBRECIPIENT:YMPJ WILL PROVIDE A SUBAWARD TO HABITATMAP, WHICH IS A NON-PROFIT BUILDING ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING AND DATA VISUALIZATION TOOLS THAT EMPOWER ORGANIZATIONS AND CITIZEN SCIENTISTS. THEY FOCUS ON LOW-INCOME COMMUNITIES AND COMMUNITIES OF COLOR LIVING WITH DISPROPORTIONATE ENVIRONMENTAL BURDENS. MICHAEL HEIMBINDER, FOUNDER AND EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR, INVENTED THE AIRBEAM AND AIRCAST 5 TECHNOLOGY ESSENTIAL TO THIS PROJECT. HABITAT MAP WILL SUPPORT THE PROJECT BY ANALYZING THE AIR QUALITY DATA COLLECTED BY YMPJ SINCE 2009 AND OVERLAYING THE AIR QUALITY DATA WITH PUBLIC HEALTH DATA INCLUDING COVID-19 TRANSMISSION AND SEVERITY RATES TO DETERMINE CORRELATIONS, AND INCIDENCE OF OTHER RESPIRATORY ISSUES. THEY WILL ALSO ASSIST IN DEVELOPING THE QAPP REQUIRED FOR THIS PROJECT. FINALLY, HABITAT MAP WILL CONTRIBUTE KEY GUEST SPEAKERS AT THE NEIGHBORHOOD COALITION STAKEHOLDER MEETINGS AND PARTICIPATE IN THE CULMINATING SYMPOSIUM. THEY HAVE A VESTED INTEREST IN THE PROJECT'S SUCCESS AND WILL CONTINUE COLLABORATING WITH YMPJ AS WE APPLY THEIR TECHNOLOGY TO PURSUE ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE GOALS.OUTCOMES:THE DELIVERABLES OF THIS PROJECT ARE: AIR QUALITY AND COVID-19 'FAST FACTS', SOCIAL MEDIA POST INCORPORATING THE FAST FACTS AND ENGAGING THE LOCAL COMMUNITY IN A DISCUSSION AROUND AIR QUALITY AND COVID-19, A COMPARISON OF SOUTH BRONX AND NEIGHBORING COMMUNITIES' DATA TO IDENTIFY DISPARATE AIR QUALITY AND HEALTH IMPACTS, A VIRTUAL SYMPOSIUM FOCUSING ON AIR QUALITY, COVID-19 OUTCOMES, AND COMMUNITY, LOCAL, STATE, AND FEDERAL ACTIONS THAT MUST BE TAKEN TO IMPROVE CONDITIONS IN THE SOUTH BRONX, A

THIS PROJECT INTENDS TO PROVIDE THESE OPPORTUNITIES, THROUGH AND WITH LOCAL STAKEHOLDERS AND PARTNERS, TO SEVERAL UNDERSERVED, ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE COMMUNITIES IN STATEN ISLAND, NY. THIS LEARNING SERIES WILL NOT ONLY PROVIDE RESIDENTS WITH ACCESS TO INFORMATION TO IMPROVE THEIR OWN QUALITY OF LIVING BUT WILL ALSO SERVE AS AN INTRODUCTION TO AN INDUSTRY THAT CURRENTLY OFFERS A HOST OF SUSTAINABLE, ENTRY-LEVEL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITIES, WITH CLEAR CAREER PATHWAYS. INCREASE IN KNOWLEDGE REGARDING TESTING, AIR QUALITY AND OTHER RELATED ITEMS. GOAL TO WORK WITH 5 LOCAL ORGANIZATION, BUSINESSES, STAKEHOLDERS TO PREPARE PARTICIPANTS FOR TESTING, TRAINING. INCREASE IN EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITIES IN THE UNDERSERVED COMMUNITY AS IT PERTAINS TO TESTING AND RELATED AREAS. EPA 608 CERTIFICATION. GOAL TO HAVE 20 INDIVIDUALS CERTIFIED IN CERTIFICATIONS.

grants.description:
DESCRIPTION:THE PURPOSE OF THIS AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN (ARP) FUNDED COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT IS TO PROVIDE FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE TO THE ST. CROIX FOUNDATION FOR COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT FOR A COMMUNITY DRIVEN PROJECT THAT WILL PROVIDE THE COMMUNITY WITH DATA AND INFORMATION ON HEALTH AND ENVIRONMENTAL RISK AND RISK MITIGATION BEST PRACTICES. ALSO, WITH A PARTNERSHIP WITH THE MARINE BIOLOGY PROGRAM AND ECO SCHOOL CLUB AT ST. CROIX CENTRAL HIGH SCHOOL, THE ECO SCHOOL CLUB AT THE ST. CROIX EDUCATIONAL COMPLEX AND UNDERGRADUATE RESEARCHERS IN COOPERATION WITH CHEMISTRY DEPARTMENT AT THE UNIVERSITY OF THE VIRGIN ISLANDS ALBERT A. SHEEN CAMPUS IN ST. CROIX, THIS PROJECT WILL TRAIN STUDENTS FOR TO CONDUCT MONITORING, SAMPLE COLLECTION AND PUBLIC EDUCATION IN ACCORDANCE WITH FEDERAL STATUTES CLEAN AIR ACT, SECTION 103(B)(3) AND CLEAN WATER ACT, SECTION 104(B)(3).ACTIVITIES:THIS PROJECT WILL ESTABLISH AIR QUALITY-ASTHMA MONITORING SYSTEM AND SUPPORT THE ONGOING WATER QUALITY MONITORING AND ESTABLISH A COMMUNITY STEERING COMMITTEE OF LOCAL COMMUNITY ADVOCATES AND CONCERNED RESIDENTS TO GUIDE PROJECT ACTIVITIES. ESTABLISH AN INNOVATIVE COMMUNITY AIR MONITORING NETWORK OF MONITORS THROUGHOUT THE TARGET AREAS OF THE ISLAND. THE PROJECT WILL DEVELOP AN AIR MONITORING PROGRAM THAT PRODUCES DATA THAT ARE SCIENTIFICALLY VALID AND USEFUL TO THE COMMUNITY. THE PROJECT WILL DETERMINE THE TECHNOLOGY TO BE USED BASED ON NEED, COSTS AND USER CAPACITY SUCH AS PURPLEAIR MONITORS, GRAB SAMPLES/BUCKET BRIGADE, FENCELINE MONITORING, TEMPORARY STATIONARY MONITORING, MOBILE MONITORING, OR A CAMN NETWORK. 

THIS PROJECT WILL RESULT IN REAL-TIME, LOCAL AIR QUALITY DATA THAT CAN ALSO BE USED IN SCIENTIFIC ANALYSIS; EDUCATION AND OUTREACH TO THE COMMUNITY UTILIZING VARIOUS MEDIA INCLUDING PRINT, SOCIAL MEDIA, WEBSITE, PUBLISHING AND DISTRIBUTE PRINTED BROCHURES, AND TOWNHALL MEETINGS. THE LONG TERM GOAL IS TO ESTABLISH A NETWORK OF AIR MONITORS THAT ARE INSTALLED AT BUILDINGS OR OTHER SITES WITHIN THE SELECTED COMMUNITY. THE MONITORS CONTINUOUSLY MEASURE LEVELS OF SPECIFIC AIR POLLUTANTS AND SEND THAT INFORMATION OVER THE INTERNET TO A SERVER, WHERE THE DATA ARE STORED IN A DATABASE.SUBRECIPIENT:THE RECIPIENT INTENDS TO ISSUE SUBAWARD AGREEMENTS TO ITS PARTNERS IN COMPLIANCE WITH APPENDIX A OF EPA'S SUBAWARD POLICY. THE SUB-AWARDEES WILL PROVIDE COORDINATION FOR PROJECT ACTIVITIES, PROVIDE TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE, AND LEAD THE AIR-MONITORING EDUCATION AND TRAINING PROGRAM.

OUTCOMES:ANTICIPATED DELIVERABLES INCLUDE REPORT AND TWO BROCHURES ON LOCAL AIR AND WATER QUALITY. EXPECTED OUTCOMES OF THIS PROJECT ARE THE DEVELOPMENT OF NEW AIR QUALITY ORDINANCES AND POLICIES ENACTED BY LOCAL GOVERNMENT; DECREASE IN THE NUMBER OF ASTHMA-RELATED HOSPITAL VISITS AMONG COMMUNITY RESIDENTS; AND AN INCREASE IN COMMUNITY DIALOGUE ABOUT ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACTS AND PUBLIC HEALTH. DIRECT BENEFICIARIES OF THIS PROJECT ARE PREDOMINANTLY RESIDENTS LOCATED IN LOW INCOME/HIGH DENSITY NEIGHBORHOODS OF ST. CROIX.

SUBRECIPIENT:NO SUBAWARDS ARE INCLUDED IN THIS ASSISTANCE AGREEMENT.OUTCOMES:EXPECTED OUTCOMES ARE AN INCREASE NUMBER OF COMMUNITY STAKEHOLDERS COMMITTED TO THE FIGHT AGAINST BLIGHT; A DECREASE IN NUMBER OF ENVIRONMENTAL AND HEALTH RISKS IN THE COMMUNITY; INCREASED NUMBER OF NEW NUISANCE ABATEMENT AND CODE ENFORCEMENT ORDINANCES ENACTED BY LOCAL GOVERNMENT; AND AN INCREASED NUMBER OF REUSE AND PLACEMAKING PROJECTS THAT CONVERTED NUISANCES FOR DISASTER RESILIENCY WITHIN A THREE-YEAR PERIOD. DIRECT BENEFICIARIES OF THIS PROJECT ARE RESIDENTS OF THE THREE TARGET COMMUNITIES OF CAGUUML;ITAS, AGUAS BUENAS, RIACUTE;O PIEDRAS, SAN JUAN, AND SAN ISIDRO, CANOACUTE;VANAS THAT ARE MADE UP OF A MIX OF LOW-INCOME RURAL, URBAN, AND INFORMAL NEIGHBORHOODS. THE RECIPIENT DOES NOT INTEND TO ISSUE ANY SUBAWARDS.

grants.description: DESCRIPTION:THE AGREEMENT PROVIDES FUNDING TO NEW JERSEY DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION. SPECIFICALLY, THE RECIPIENT WILL PARTNER WITH COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS TO MAP AND IDENTIFY AREAS EXPERIENCING EXTREME HEAT AND URBAN HEAT ISLAND EFFECT, COLLECT TEMPERATURE AND AIR QUALITY DATA, CONDUCT HEAT VULNERABILITY ASSESSMENTS, AND SHARE FINDINGS WITH COMMUNITY MEMBERS. THE PROJECT WILL PROMOTE IMPROVED PUBLIC HEALTH IN COMMUNITIES WITH ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE CONCERNS AND PROVIDE COMMUNITIES WITH GRANULAR DATA AND TAILORED MITIGATION STRATEGIES TO ADDRESS EXTREME HEAT AND URBAN HEAT ISLAND EFFECT.ACTIVITIES:THE ACTIVITIES INCLUDE MAPPING AND IDENTIFYING URBAN HEAT ISLAND AREAS, COLLECTING DATA, CONDUCTING COMMUNITY-LED VULNERABILITY ASSESSMENTS, AND SHARING FINDINGS. EXISTING MAPS WILL BE EXPANDED TO IDENTIFY DATA COLLECTION ROUTES. A QUALITY ASSURANCE PROJECT PLAN WILL BE DEVELOPED, AND COMMUNITY SCIENTISTS WILL BE TRAINED IN MONITORING EQUIPMENT AND DATA COLLECTION MANAGEMENT ACTIVITIES. STATIONARY AND WEARABLE MONITORS WILL BE USED TO COLLECT TEMPERATURE, HUMIDITY, PARTICULATE MATTER, AND GROUND LEVEL OZONE DATA. DATA WILL BE REVIEWED, VALIDATED, AND ANALYZED, THEN PROVIDED TO COMMUNITY PARTNERS AND INCORPORATED INTO MAPS. A HEAT VULNERABILITY ASSESSMENT TEMPLATE WILL BE DEVELOPED. COMMUNITY SCIENTISTS WILL BE TRAINED TO IDENTIFY QUALITATIVE EXTREME HEAT INDICATORS THAT MAY BE EXACERBATED BY URBAN HEAT ISLAND EFFECT AND FILL OUT THE ASSESSMENT TEMPLATE. FINAL VULNERABILITY ASSESSMENTS AND MAPS WILL BE DEVELOPED FOR EACH SELECTED MUNICIPALITY. FINDINGS WILL BE SHARED USING TAILORED COMMUNICATION AND OUTREACH STRATEGIES. SUBRECIPIENT:SUBRECIPIENTS INCLUDE NEW JERSEY COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT CORPORATION (REPRESENTING PATERSON, PASSAIC, AND CLIFTON), GROUNDWORK ELIZABETH (REPRESENTING ELIZABETH), SOUTH WARD ENVIRONMENTAL ALLIANCE (REPRESENTING NEWARK'S SOUTH WARD), ISLES, INC. (REPRESENTING TRENTON), AND NEW JERSEY PROGRESSIVE EQUITABLE ENERGY COALITION. SUBRECIPIENTS HAVE IDENTICAL RESPONSIBILITIES FOR THE MUNICIPALITIES THEY REPRESENT, INCLUDING PROVIDING LOCAL LEADERSHIP AND INFORMATION ON COMMUNITY CONCERNS, ADVISEMENT ON HYPER-LOCAL SOCIAL FACTORS IMPACTING EXTREME HEAT AND URBAN HEAT ISLAND EFFECT, RECRUITMENT AND COORDINATION OF COMMUNITY SCIENTISTS, AIDING IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF VULNERABILITY ASSESSMENTS, AND DISSEMINATION AND COMMUNICATION OF PROJECT FINDINGS. NEW JERSEY PROGRESSIVE EQUITABLE ENERGY COALITION WILL PROVIDE ADVISORY SUPPORT ON VULNERABILITY ASSESSMENT DEVELOPMENT.OUTCOMES:THE ANTICIPATED DELIVERABLES INCLUDE STATE-WIDE STEERING AND LOCAL PROJECT TEAMS, PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENTS, A QUALITY ASSURANCE PROJECT PLAN, INITIAL MAPS WITH MONITORING ROUTES, TRAINED COMMUNITY SCIENTISTS, VALIDATED DATA, REPORTS, AND ANALYSES, A HEAT VULNERABILITY ASSESSMENT TEMPLATE, FINAL MAPS WITH HEAT, AIR QUALITY, AND VULNERABILITY ANALYSIS, HEAT VULNERABILITY ASSESSMENTS, A COMMUNICATIONS STRATEGY, AND SEMI-ANNUAL AND FINAL REPORTS. THE EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE STRENGTHENED PARTNERSHIPS BETWEEN STATE GOVERNMENT, COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS, AND ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE NONPROFITS, INCREASED CAPACITY OF MUNICIPAL GOVERNMENTS, COMMUNITY GROUPS, AND NONPROFITS TO UNDERSTAND AND ADDRESS ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE ISSUES, INCREASED AWARENESS OF ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE IN AFFECTED COMMUNITIES, AND INCREASED COMMUNITY RESILIENCY TO ALLEVIATE ENVIRONMENTAL AND PUBLIC HEALTH BURDENS. COMMUNITY PARTNERS WILL BE EQUIPPED TO RECOMMEND AND ENACT HYPER-LOCAL HEAT MITIGATION AND RESILIENCE STRATEGIES THAT LOWER TEMPERATURES AND DECREASE HEAT-RELATED ILLNESSES AND HOSPITALIZATIONS. THE RECIPIENT WILL GAIN DATA TO INFORM INITIATIVES, INSIGHT ON PUTTING FORTH LOCAL HEAT MITIGATION STRATEGIES, AND COLLABORATIVE PARTNERSHIPS TO ADDRESS URBAN HEAT ISLAND AND OTHER CLIMATE ISSUES. THE INTENDED BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE COMMUNITY SCIENTISTS, RESIDENTS, AND LOCAL LEADERS IN THE OVERBURDENED NEW JERSEY MUNICIPALITIES OF PATERSON, ELIZABETH, NEWARK, PASSAIC
